title: "Report on Transcriptome Assembly"

date: today
format:

    toc: true
    toc-location: left
    number-sections: true
    smooth-scroll: true
    embed-resources: true
    # Article layout, so prose keeps a readable measure. Figures wider than the body
    # column carry `column: page` and span the full grid instead.
    page-layout: article
    theme: cosmo
    include-in-header:
        text: |
            <style>
                .quarto-title-block .quarto-title-banner {
                background-image: url(https://i.imgur.com/ggW6gEC.png) !important;
                background-size: 250px !important;
                background-position: left 30px center !important;
                background-repeat: no-repeat !important;
                background-origin: content-box;
                }
                /* Bootstrap's .img-fluid rule does not always survive into the
                   self-contained HTML, and without it a figure lays out at its
                   natural pixel width and the page scrolls sideways. */
                img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }
            </style>
    include-after-body:
        text: |
            <style>
            #TOC .toc-title, 
            #TOC > h2, 
            #TOC > h3 {
                font-weight: bold !important;

            }
            </style>

                .report-footer {

                margin-top: 10px;
                padding-top: 10px;
                padding-bottom: 10px;
                border-top: 1px solid #dee2e6;
                }

                display: flex;
                justify-content: center;
                align-items: center;
                gap: 50px; /* space between logos */
                flex-wrap: wrap;
                }
                .footer-logos img {
                max-height: 120px; /* Adjust height as needed */
                width: auto;
                transition: opacity 0.3s ease;
                }
                    .footer-logos a:hover img {
                opacity: 0.8;
                }
            </style>

            <footer class="report-footer">
                <div class="footer-logos">
                    <img src="https://imgur.com/cbsEIqD.png" alt="Logos">
                </div>
            </footer>
execute:
    echo: false
    warning: false
    message: false
    error: true

    counts_genes: "BambuOutput_counts_gene_validated.txt"

    novel_protein_coding_exonlength: "novel_protein-coding_exon_lengths.csv"


```{r}

library(ggplot2)

base_theme <- theme(

  plot.title = element_text(size = rel(1.3), margin = margin(b = 8)),

  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#e5e5e5", linewidth = 0.3),

  panel.border = element_rect(color = "#4d4d4d", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
  axis.line = element_line(color = "#4d4d4d", linewidth = 0.3),
  axis.ticks = element_line( color = "#4d4d4d", linewidth = 0.3),


  legend.background = element_blank(),
  # Compact legends and tight outer margins: these figures also go on a poster,
  # where every millimetre of white space around a panel is wasted.
  legend.key.size    = unit(0.75, "lines"),
  legend.box.spacing = unit(10, "pt"),
  legend.margin      = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
  legend.key = element_blank(),

  plot.margin = margin(4, 6, 4, 4)
)

theme_set(
  theme_bw(base_family = "Source Sans 3", base_size = 10) +
    base_theme)

update_geom_defaults("text",
  list(family = "Source Sans 3", size = 8 / .pt, colour = "#222222")
)

update_geom_defaults(
  "label",
  list(family = "Source Sans 3", size = 8 / .pt, colour = "#222222",
    fill = "white", label.size = 0.2)
)

# --- Shared log axes ---------------------------------------------------------
# Every log-scaled axis in this report goes through these, so tick labels read
# 1,000 rather than a mixture of 1,000 and 1e+03.
#
# expand_top adds headroom above the highest bar. Set it wherever count labels
# are drawn on top of bars, otherwise the topmost label is clipped by the panel
# edge.

scale_y_log10_std <- function(expand_top = FALSE, ...) {
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = scales::breaks_log(),
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    expand = if (expand_top) expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25)) else waiver(),
    ...
  )
}

scale_x_log10_std <- function(...) {
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = scales::breaks_log(),
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    ...
  )
}

# Exon counts are small integers, so the default log breaks (1, 3, 10, 30) read
# oddly for a number of exons. Force integer breaks instead. The axis stays
# logarithmic because the distribution is heavily skewed towards 1-2 exons.
scale_y_log10_exons <- function(...) {
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200),
    labels = scales::label_comma(accuracy = 1),
    ...
  )
}

# --- Palette -----------------------------------------------------------------

options(
  # "viridis", spelled out: this read option = "P", which viridisLite does not
  # have and silently replaced with viridis anyway.
  ggplot2.discrete.fill = function(...) scale_fill_viridis_d(..., option = "viridis", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8),
  ggplot2.discrete.colour = function(...) scale_colour_viridis_d(..., option = "viridis", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8)
)

# --- Chromosome ordering -----------------------------------------------------
# Facet chromosomes in genomic order (1, 2, ... 10, 11 ... X, Y, MT) rather than
# the alphabetical order a plain sort() gives, which would interleave 10 and 11
# between 1 and 2.
#
# The optional chr prefix is stripped before the numeric test. Ensembl names
# contigs "1" while GENCODE names them "chr1"; without stripping, no GENCODE
# name matches the numeric pattern and every chromosome falls through to the
# alphabetical branch.

order_chromosomes <- function(x) {
  values <- unique(as.character(x))
  bare <- sub("^chr", "", values, ignore.case = TRUE)

  is_numeric_chr <- grepl("^[0-9]+$", bare)
  numeric_sorted <- values[is_numeric_chr][order(as.numeric(bare[is_numeric_chr]))]
  other_sorted <- sort(values[!is_numeric_chr])

  # droplevels so a chromosome absent from the data never reserves an empty panel
  droplevels(factor(x, levels = c(numeric_sorted, other_sorted)))
}

# --- Chromosome distribution figures -----------------------------------------
# Ensembl and GENCODE both mix hundreds of unplaced contigs (GL000195.1,
# KI270728.1) in with the real chromosomes. On a GENCODE v50 run, 47 of 72
# seqnames were scaffolds carrying 1-12 transcripts each. Pattern rather than a
# fixed list: the pipeline runs on any Ensembl/GENCODE organism, so this also has
# to cover roman-numeral (yeast I-XVI), arm-suffixed (fly 2L/3R) and organelle
# names.
is_assembled_chromosome <- function(x) {
  bare <- toupper(sub("^chr", "", as.character(x), ignore.case = TRUE))
  grepl("^([0-9]{1,2}[A-Z]?|[IVXL]{1,6}|[XYZW]|M|MT|MITO|MTDNA|PT|PLTD)$", bare)
}

# --- Shared palettes ---------------------------------------------------------
# One colour map per report section, so a reader can tell at a glance which part
# of the report a figure belongs to:
#
#   Assembly Statistics                          -> turbo
#   Isoform Diversity per Gene                   -> turbo
#   Reference Transcriptome                      -> viridis
#   Novel Isoforms (and Tracking Evidence)       -> plasma
#
# Within a section, colours are fixed per category name, so a novel lncRNA
# candidate is the same colour in every novel figure.
VIR_FULL <- function(n) viridis::viridis(n, end = 0.9)
VIR_MID  <- function(n) viridis::viridis(n, begin = 0.2, end = 0.8)
PLA_FULL <- function(n) viridis::plasma(n, end = 0.85)
PLA_MID  <- function(n) viridis::plasma(n, begin = 0.15, end = 0.75)
TUR_FULL <- function(n) viridis::turbo(n, begin = 0.1, end = 0.9)

# Novel section: plasma.
NOVEL_COLOURS <- c(
  setNames(PLA_FULL(3), c("novel lncRNA candidate", "predicted non-coding",
                          "predicted protein-coding")),
  `novel (unclassified)` = "#9E9E9E"
)

# Reference section: viridis.
ANN_BIOTYPE_COLOURS <- setNames(VIR_FULL(5), c("protein_coding", "lncRNA", "small_RNA",
                                               "pseudogene", "other"))

# Assembly section: turbo.
STATUS_COLOURS <- setNames(TUR_FULL(3), c("Total", "Annotated", "Novel"))

SUPPORT_LEVELS  <- c("full-length + unique", "unique only", "full-length only", "neither")
SUPPORT_COLOURS <- setNames(TUR_FULL(4), SUPPORT_LEVELS)
SUPPORT_TEXT    <- setNames(c("white", "#222222", "#222222", "white"), SUPPORT_LEVELS)
# The same four levels in the novel section's plasma, with text colours to match.
SUPPORT_COLOURS_NOVEL <- setNames(PLA_FULL(4), SUPPORT_LEVELS)
SUPPORT_TEXT_NOVEL    <- setNames(c("white", "white", "#222222", "#222222"), SUPPORT_LEVELS)

SMALL_RNA_BIOTYPES <- c("snoRNA", "snRNA", "scaRNA", "sRNA", "rRNA", "misc_RNA", "miRNA")

# A named colour vector covering exactly `lv`: named entries from `pal` where they
# exist, viridis for anything the palette does not know.
# A single unnamed colour paints every level.
palette_for <- function(lv, pal = NULL) {
  lv  <- as.character(lv)
  if (!is.null(pal) && is.null(names(pal))) return(setNames(rep(pal[1], length(lv)), lv))
  out <- if (is.null(pal)) character(0) else pal[intersect(lv, names(pal))]
  miss <- setdiff(lv, names(out))
  if (length(miss)) {
    out <- c(out, setNames(viridis::viridis(length(miss), end = 0.85), miss))
  }
  out[lv]
}

# Compact axis labels: 1,000 -> 1k, 100,000 -> 100k. Tick labels on narrow facets
# collide at full width; data labels keep the full comma form.
short_number <- function(x) {
  vapply(x, function(v) {
    if (is.na(v))      return(NA_character_)
    # Breaks come back through the pseudo-log inverse with float noise
    # (999,999.99...), which read as "1000k" instead of "1M".
    v <- signif(v, 6)
    if (abs(v) >= 1e6) return(paste0(as.character(signif(v / 1e6, 3)), "M"))
    if (abs(v) >= 1e3) return(paste0(as.character(signif(v / 1e3, 3)), "k"))
    as.character(signif(v, 3))
  }, character(1))
}

# Gap between a point and its printed count. hjust alone scales the gap with the
# width of the label, so a one-digit count touched its point; a fixed run of
# spaces keeps the same gap whatever the number.
LABEL_PAD <- strrep(" ", 4)

# --- Count lollipops ---------------------------------------------------------
# Counts of one categorical variable (`x`), drawn HORIZONTALLY: categories run
# down the y axis so long names (chromosomes, biotypes, classifications) are read
# unrotated, and each count is printed to the right of its point.
#
#   y      -> one facet COLUMN per level, each with its own count axis
#   facet  -> optional facet ROWS; each row shows only the categories observed in it
#
# The count axis is a pseudo-log. `scales::pseudo_log_trans` is log-like above 1
# but, unlike log10, is defined at zero, so a category with no transcripts sits on
# the baseline as a hollow point labelled 0. Missing combinations are completed to
# zero rather than dropped, because a chromosome carrying none of a biotype is a
# real measurement.
#
# `df` needs one row per cell with a `count` column.
COUNT_TRANS <- scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 1, base = 10)

# Breaks for the pseudo-log axis. 0 and 1 sit only 0.2 decades apart, so 1 is
# dropped once the axis spans two decades or more, and alternate decades are
# dropped when there would be more than four -- otherwise the labels overprint
# on a narrow facet.
count_breaks <- function(lims) {
  hi <- max(lims, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(hi) || hi <= 0) return(0)
  # `lims` includes the 55% of right-hand headroom plot_count_lollipop() leaves for
  # the count labels. Ticks only need to reach the data, so undo it: ticks drawn
  # out to the edge ("0 10 100 1k" on a panel whose largest count is 247)
  # overprinted on narrow panels.
  hi <- COUNT_TRANS$inverse(COUNT_TRANS$transform(hi) / 1.55)
  if (hi < 10) {
    b <- c(0, 1, 2, 5)
    return(b[b <= max(hi, 1) * 1.001])
  }
  # From 10 up, 0 and 1 sit a fifth of a decade apart, so 1 is never labelled.
  dec <- 10^(1:8)
  dec <- dec[dec <= hi * 1.001]
  if (length(dec) > 3) dec <- rev(rev(dec)[seq(1, length(dec), by = 2)])
  c(0, dec)
}

plot_count_lollipop <- function(df, x, y, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                                x_lab = NULL, count_lab = "Transcripts",
                                facet = NULL, colours = NULL,
                                colour_by = c("col", "row"),
                                complete_grid = TRUE, strip_wrap = 15) {

  # colour_by = "row" colours points by the facet row instead of the column, for
  # figures whose rows are the routed categories.
  colour_by <- match.arg(colour_by)

  d <- dplyr::transmute(df,
                        .cat  = {{ x }},
                        .col  = {{ y }},
                        .row  = if (is.null(facet)) "" else .data[[facet]],
                        count = count)

  # nesting(.row, .cat): a facet row is completed only over the categories actually
  # observed in it, so a gene biotype's row never lists another biotype's
  # transcript biotypes. Every column is completed, so zeros stay visible.
  if (complete_grid) {
    d <- tidyr::complete(d, tidyr::nesting(.row, .cat), .col, fill = list(count = 0))
  }

  # Category order: a factor (chromosomes) keeps its order, first level on top;
  # anything else is ordered by total count, largest on top.
  if (is.factor(d$.cat)) {
    d$.cat <- factor(d$.cat, levels = rev(levels(droplevels(d$.cat))))
  } else {
    tot    <- tapply(d$count, as.character(d$.cat), sum)
    d$.cat <- factor(d$.cat, levels = names(sort(tot)))
  }
  if (!is.factor(d$.col)) d$.col <- factor(d$.col)
  d$.col <- droplevels(d$.col)
  if (!is.factor(d$.row)) d$.row <- factor(d$.row)
  d$.row <- droplevels(d$.row)
  d$.clr <- if (colour_by == "row") d$.row else d$.col

  cols <- palette_for(levels(d$.clr), colours)

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(y = .cat, x = count)) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = count, yend = .cat, colour = .clr), linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = .clr, shape = count > 0), size = 2,
               fill = "white", stroke = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(LABEL_PAD, scales::comma(count))),
              hjust = 0, size = 7.5 / .pt) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 19, `FALSE` = 21), guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cols, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(trans  = COUNT_TRANS,
                       breaks = count_breaks,
                       labels = short_number,
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.55))) +
    # Labels may run past the panel edge on the widest count; clip = "off" lets them
    # into the facet gutter instead of cutting them.
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(.row), cols = vars(.col),
               scales = "free", space = "free_y",
               labeller = labeller(.col = label_wrap_gen(strip_wrap),
                                   .row = label_wrap_gen(16))) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#ececec", linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing.x    = unit(1.6, "lines"),
      panel.spacing.y    = unit(0.6, "lines"),
      strip.text.y       = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
      axis.text.y        = element_text(size = rel(0.9)),
      plot.title         = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = count_lab, y = x_lab)

  if (is.null(facet))               p <- p + theme(strip.text.y = element_blank())
  if (nlevels(d$.col) == 1 &&
      identical(levels(d$.col), "")) p <- p + theme(strip.text.x = element_blank())
  p
}

# Figure width (inches) for a lollipop with `n_cols` facet columns: room for the
# longest category label on the left, ~1.15 in per panel, and the row strips.
lollipop_width <- function(n_cols, y_labels, row_strips = TRUE) {
  lab <- 0.063 * max(nchar(as.character(y_labels)), 4)
  min(13, max(4, 0.5 + lab + 1.15 * n_cols + if (row_strips) 1.2 else 0.2))
}

# Figure height (inches) for a lollipop with `n` category rows.
lollipop_height <- function(n, base = 1.3, per = 0.2) max(2.2, base + per * n)

plot_chr_distribution <- function(df, title, subtitle, colours = NULL) {
  plot_count_lollipop(df, x = chromosome, y = biotype,
                      title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
                      x_lab = "Chromosome", colours = colours)
}

# --- Mono- vs multi-exonic composition --------------------------------------
# Two bars side by side per category (classification, transcript biotype):
# mono-exonic and multi-exonic transcripts, one facet panel per group (routed
# category, gene biotype). Each panel lists only the categories that group
# actually has. A category with no transcripts of one exon class keeps that bar
# at zero, labelled 0, so every pair reads the same way.
#
# The count axis is the same pseudo-log as the lollipops: counts run from single
# digits to six figures, and on a linear axis every mono-exonic bar but one was
# invisible. Each bar's count is printed vertically above it, so neighbouring
# labels never collide.
EXON_CLASS_COLOURS       <- setNames(VIR_MID(2), c("mono-exonic", "multi-exonic"))
EXON_CLASS_COLOURS_NOVEL <- setNames(PLA_MID(2), c("mono-exonic", "multi-exonic"))

plot_exon_class_bars <- function(df, x, facet, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                                 x_lab = NULL, count_lab = "Transcripts",
                                 strip_wrap = 18, label_wrap = 16,
                                 colours = EXON_CLASS_COLOURS) {
  d <- dplyr::transmute(df,
                        .cat       = as.character({{ x }}),
                        .fac       = .data[[facet]],
                        class_exon = factor(class_exon, levels = names(EXON_CLASS_COLOURS)),
                        count      = count) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.fac, .cat, class_exon) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(count = sum(count), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::complete(tidyr::nesting(.fac, .cat), class_exon, fill = list(count = 0))
  if (!is.factor(d$.fac)) d$.fac <- factor(d$.fac)
  d$.fac <- droplevels(d$.fac)

  # Largest category first within each panel. A category can appear under
  # several groups, so the x key is made unique per group and the group prefix
  # is stripped again for the axis labels.
  tot  <- d %>% dplyr::group_by(.fac, .cat) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(total = sum(count), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::arrange(.fac, dplyr::desc(total))
  keys <- paste(tot$.fac, tot$.cat, sep = "\u001f")
  d$.key <- factor(paste(d$.fac, d$.cat, sep = "\u001f"), levels = keys)

  # Rotated labels hang down and to the LEFT of their tick, so the first label
  # can run past the plot edge; the left margin is sized for it.
  wrap_lab <- function(k) vapply(sub("^.*\u001f", "", k), function(z)
    paste(strwrap(gsub("_", " ", z), label_wrap), collapse = "\n"), character(1),
    USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  first_w <- max(nchar(strsplit(wrap_lab(keys[1]), "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]))
  left_pt <- max(4, 0.707 * 4.2 * first_w - 30)
  pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.8)

  ggplot(d, aes(x = .key, y = count, fill = class_exon)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.75, position = pd) +
    geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(count), group = class_exon), position = pd,
              angle = 90, hjust = -0.15, size = 6 / .pt, colour = "#222222") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colours, drop = FALSE, name = "Exon structure") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = wrap_lab) +
    scale_y_continuous(trans = COUNT_TRANS, breaks = count_breaks, labels = short_number,
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.55))) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    facet_grid(cols = vars(.fac), scales = "free_x", space = "free_x",
               labeller = labeller(.fac = label_wrap_gen(strip_wrap))) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#ececec", linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.spacing.x    = unit(0.5, "lines"),
      axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1,
                                        size = rel(0.85), lineheight = 0.85),
      plot.margin        = margin(4, 6, 4, left_pt),
      legend.position    = "right",
      plot.title         = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = x_lab, y = paste(count_lab, "(pseudo-log)"))
}

# Figure width (inches) for plot_exon_class_bars() with `n` bars in total.
exon_bars_width <- function(n) min(11, max(4, 2.2 + 0.5 * n))

# --- Per-gene count helpers ----------------------------------------------------
# Shared by the rank curves and the top-gene tables in Isoform Diversity per Gene.
ISOFORM_BREAKS <- c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000)

# Label positions at least `gap` apart (log10 units), in the same order as `y`,
# re-centred on the points so the block of labels sits beside them. geom_text
# has no repel, and ggrepel is not a dependency of this report.
spread_labels <- function(y, gap) {
  if (length(y) < 2) return(y)
  o <- order(y, decreasing = TRUE)
  z <- y[o]
  for (i in seq_along(z)[-1]) z[i] <- min(z[i], z[i - 1] - gap)
  z <- z + (mean(y[o]) - mean(z))
  if (min(z) < 0) z <- z - min(z)          # never below 1 isoform
  out <- numeric(length(y)); out[o] <- z
  out
}

# Axis labels for category names: underscores to spaces so they can wrap.
wrap_cat <- function(width = 12) {
  function(x) vapply(gsub("_", " ", x), function(z) paste(strwrap(z, width), collapse = "\n"),
                     character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}


# --- Rank curve ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Genes ranked by a per-gene count, most first, one step line per group, one
# panel per facet. Suited to small-integer counts with a long tail (novel isoforms
# per gene): the flat run at 1 and the few genes far above it are both read
# directly, with no density smoothing. Log x, so the top of the ranking gets the
# room; the top `n_top` genes of each panel are named in the empty upper right,
# which a decaying curve always leaves free.
#
# `genes`: one row per gene with gene, value, .x (line group) and .fac (panel).
RANK_BREAKS <- 10^(0:6)

plot_rank_curve <- function(genes, colours, n_top = 5, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                            y_lab = "Isoforms per gene", colour_lab = "Gene biotype",
                            legend = TRUE) {
  g <- genes %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.fac, .x) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(value), gene, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(rank = dplyr::row_number(), n_genes = dplyr::n()) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  # Top genes per panel, across its lines; ties broken by name. Each is marked
  # with a diamond on its curve and listed in the panel's top-right corner,
  # coloured like its curve: a decaying curve always leaves that corner empty.
  # Numbering the diamonds was dropped -- the top genes of different biotypes
  # often share a rank and a count, so their numbers printed on top of each other.
  top <- g %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.fac) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(value), gene, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = n_top) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(i     = dplyr::row_number(),
                  entry = sprintf("%s (%s)", gene, scales::comma(value)),
                  # One text row per entry, stacked down from the corner.
                  vj    = 1.5 + 1.35 * (i - 1)) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  few <- dplyr::filter(g, n_genes < 3)

  ggplot(g, aes(x = rank, y = value, colour = .x)) +
    geom_step(direction = "hv", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(data = few, size = 1.3) +
    geom_point(data = top, shape = 23, size = 1.8, fill = "white", stroke = 0.7) +
    geom_text(data = top, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = entry, vjust = vj, colour = .x),
              hjust = 1.04, size = 6 / .pt, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = colours, name = colour_lab, drop = TRUE) +
    # Decades only: 1, 10, 100, 1k, 10k. Every 1-2-5 step overprinted on a
    # narrow panel.
    scale_x_log10(breaks = RANK_BREAKS, labels = short_number,
                  expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.04))) +
    # Headroom above the highest step, so the corner list sits above the curve.
    scale_y_log10(breaks = ISOFORM_BREAKS, labels = scales::label_comma(accuracy = 1),
                  expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.45))) +
    facet_wrap(~ .fac, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x",
               labeller = labeller(.fac = label_wrap_gen(22))) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.2, shape = NA))) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "#ececec", linewidth = 0.25),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#e5e5e5", linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.25),
      panel.spacing.x    = unit(0.9, "lines"),
      # No legend when each panel is one line: the strip already names it.
      legend.position    = if (legend) "right" else "none",
      plot.title         = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = "Gene rank (log10)", y = y_lab)
}

# Top `n` genes per group, largest first, ties broken by name so the choice is
# reproducible. `n_tied` says how many genes share the n-th value, for the table.
top_genes <- function(d, n = 5) {
  d %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(c(".fac", ".x")))) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(value), gene, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(rank   = dplyr::row_number(),
                  cutoff = value[min(n, dplyr::n())],
                  n_tied = sum(value == cutoff)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(rank <= n) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(label = sprintf("%s (%s)", gene, scales::comma(value)))
}

# --- Isoforms-per-gene bins --------------------------------------------------
# The same per-gene counts as the rank curves, binned and drawn as 100% stacked
# bars. Isoform counts are small integers, which a violin smooths into bumps;
# bins give the exact share of genes at 1, 2, 3-5, 6-10 and more isoforms.
ISO_BIN_LEVELS  <- c("1", "2", "3–5", "6–10", ">10")
# Isoform Diversity section: turbo, blue (1 isoform) to red (>10).
ISO_BIN_COLOURS <- setNames(TUR_FULL(5), ISO_BIN_LEVELS)
ISO_BIN_TEXT    <- setNames(c("white", "#222222", "#222222", "#222222", "white"), ISO_BIN_LEVELS)

iso_bin <- function(v) {
  factor(as.character(cut(v, c(0, 1, 2, 5, 10, Inf), labels = ISO_BIN_LEVELS)),
         levels = ISO_BIN_LEVELS)
}

# `genes`: one row per gene with .x (group), value, and optionally .fac (facet row).
plot_isoform_bins <- function(genes, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                              fill_lab = "Isoforms\nper gene") {
  has_fac <- ".fac" %in% names(genes)
  if (!has_fac) genes$.fac <- factor("")
  d <- genes %>%
    dplyr::mutate(bin = iso_bin(value)) %>%
    dplyr::count(.fac, .x, bin, name = "n") %>%
    tidyr::complete(.fac, .x, bin, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.fac, .x) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(n_grp = sum(n), frac = ifelse(n_grp > 0, n / n_grp, 0)) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::filter(n_grp > 0)

  # Group name and gene count on the axis, first group on top in every row.
  d <- dplyr::arrange(d, .fac, .x)
  d$.lab <- sprintf("%s\n(n = %s)", d$.x, scales::comma(d$n_grp))
  d$.lab <- factor(d$.lab, levels = rev(unique(d$.lab)))

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = frac, y = .lab, fill = bin)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.78, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(frac >= 0.1, scales::percent(frac, accuracy = 1), ""),
                  colour = bin),
              position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
              size = 6.5 / .pt, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = ISO_BIN_COLOURS, drop = FALSE, name = fill_lab) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = ISO_BIN_TEXT, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = c("0", "", "50%", "", "100%"), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                       expand = c(0, 0)) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y        = element_text(size = rel(0.85), lineheight = 0.9),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#ececec", linewidth = 0.3),
      strip.text.y       = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
      legend.position    = "right",
      plot.title         = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = "Share of genes", y = NULL)

  if (has_fac) {
    p <- p + facet_grid(rows = vars(.fac), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y",
                        labeller = labeller(.fac = label_wrap_gen(14)))
  }
  p
}

# --- Read-support composition ------------------------------------------------
# Full-length and unique support are two memberships, so each transcript falls in
# exactly one of four combinations. Drawn as 100% stacked horizontal bars, one per
# group: proportions keep a 1,000-transcript novel group readable next to a
# 190,000-transcript annotated one, which the UpSet's absolute bars could not.
# Exact counts go in the companion table (support_table()).
support_class <- function(fl, uq) {
  fl <- !is.na(fl) & fl
  uq <- !is.na(uq) & uq
  factor(dplyr::case_when(fl & uq ~ SUPPORT_LEVELS[1],
                          uq      ~ SUPPORT_LEVELS[2],
                          fl      ~ SUPPORT_LEVELS[3],
                          TRUE    ~ SUPPORT_LEVELS[4]),
         levels = SUPPORT_LEVELS)
}

support_counts <- function(df, group) {
  d <- dplyr::mutate(df,
                     .grp    = {{ group }},
                     support = support_class(`full-length support`, `unique support`))
  if (!is.factor(d$.grp)) d$.grp <- factor(d$.grp)
  d$.grp <- droplevels(d$.grp)
  d %>%
    dplyr::count(.grp, support, name = "n") %>%
    tidyr::complete(.grp, support, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.grp) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(n_grp = sum(n), frac = ifelse(n_grp > 0, n / n_grp, 0)) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
}

plot_support_bars <- function(df, group, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL, y_lab = NULL,
                              label_wrap = 20, colours = SUPPORT_COLOURS,
                              text_colours = SUPPORT_TEXT) {
  d <- support_counts(df, {{ group }})
  # Group name (wrapped, so long classification names do not widen the figure)
  # and size on the axis; first group on top.
  grp  <- dplyr::arrange(dplyr::distinct(d, .grp, n_grp), .grp)
  labs_by_grp <- setNames(sprintf("%s\n(n = %s)",
                                  vapply(as.character(grp$.grp), function(z)
                                    paste(strwrap(z, label_wrap), collapse = "\n"),
                                    character(1)),
                                  scales::comma(grp$n_grp)),
                          as.character(grp$.grp))
  d$.lab <- factor(unname(labs_by_grp[as.character(d$.grp)]),
                   levels = rev(unname(labs_by_grp)))

  ggplot(d, aes(x = frac, y = .lab, fill = support)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.78, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
    # Labelled only where the segment is wide enough to hold the text at the
    # compact width these figures are drawn at.
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(frac >= 0.1, scales::percent(frac, accuracy = 1), ""),
                  colour = support),
              position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
              size = 6.5 / .pt, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colours, drop = FALSE, name = "Read support",
                      labels = c("full-length\n+ unique", "unique only",
                                 "full-length only", "neither")) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = text_colours, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = c("0", "", "50%", "", "100%"), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                       expand = c(0, 0)) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y        = element_text(size = rel(0.85), lineheight = 0.9),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#ececec", linewidth = 0.3),
      legend.position    = "right",
      plot.title         = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = "Share of transcripts", y = y_lab)
}

# Exact counts behind plot_support_bars(), as a markdown table inside a <details>.
support_table <- function(df, group, group_name) {
  tab <- support_counts(df, {{ group }}) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(cell = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", scales::comma(n), 100 * frac)) %>%
    dplyr::select(.grp, n_grp, support, cell) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = support, values_from = cell) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Total = scales::comma(n_grp)) %>%
    dplyr::select(-n_grp)
  names(tab)[1] <- group_name
  cat("<details><summary>Exact counts</summary>\n\n")
  cat(knitr::kable(tab, format = "markdown"), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n\n</details>\n\n")
}

bar_height <- function(n_groups, base = 0.9, per = 0.34) max(1.5, base + per * n_groups)

# A category with no rows is dropped rather than drawn as an empty panel. Returns
# the named list with every zero-row entry removed.
drop_empty_groups <- function(groups) {
  keep <- vapply(groups, function(g) !is.null(g) && nrow(g) > 0, logical(1))
  groups[keep]
}

# --- UpSet ------------------------------------------------------------------
# ComplexUpset, wrapped so every call site gets the same axis, ordering and
# annotation treatment. Kept only where the sets are genuinely non-exclusive and
# there are enough of them for intersections to be worth reading (Bambu
# transcript classes, warning signs). Two-set support questions use
# plot_support_bars() instead.
#
# Sets must be attributes an item can hold *simultaneously*. Mutually exclusive
# categories -- biotype, class code, chromosome -- are not sets: they belong in
# `fill_col`, which stacks each bar.
#
# `df` needs one row per item, a logical column per entry in `sets`, and
# optionally `fill_col` naming a categorical column. `show_empty = FALSE` drops
# the "none of these sets" bar, for figures where it dwarfs everything else; the
# caller reports that count in the subtitle instead.
plot_upset <- function(df, sets, fill_col = NULL, fill_values = NULL,
                       title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                       max_intersections = 12, show_empty = TRUE) {

  placeholder <- function(msg) {
    ggplot() +
      annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = msg, colour = "grey25") +
      theme_void() +
      labs(title = title) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
  }

  if (is.null(df) || !nrow(df)) return(placeholder("No transcripts to plot."))

  present <- sets[vapply(sets, function(s) s %in% names(df), logical(1))]
  if (!length(present)) {
    return(placeholder(sprintf("None of the expected columns are present: %s.",
                               paste(sets, collapse = ", "))))
  }

  d <- as.data.frame(df, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (s in present) d[[s]] <- !is.na(d[[s]]) & as.logical(d[[s]])

  has_fill <- !is.null(fill_col) && fill_col %in% names(d)
  if (has_fill) d[[fill_col]] <- droplevels(factor(d[[fill_col]]))

  size_layer <- if (has_fill) {
    ComplexUpset::intersection_size(
      counts = TRUE, text = list(vjust = -0.5),
      bar_number_threshold = Inf,
      mapping = ggplot2::aes(fill = .data[[fill_col]]))
  } else {
    ComplexUpset::intersection_size(
      counts = TRUE, text = list(vjust = -0.5),
      bar_number_threshold = Inf)
  }

  size_layer <- size_layer +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
      expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18)),
      labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ","))

  if (has_fill) {
    size_layer <- size_layer +
      ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
        values = palette_for(levels(d[[fill_col]]), fill_values), name = NULL)
  }

  # Set sizes: the count is printed just past the end of each bar (outside it, in
  # dark text) and the axis gets headroom for it. Printed inside in white, the
  # label was cut off by short bars. Axis ticks use the compact 100k form so the
  # four tick labels no longer run into one another.
  set_size_layer <- ComplexUpset::upset_set_size(position = "right") +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = ggplot2::after_stat(scales::comma(count))),
                       stat = "count", hjust = -0.15, colour = "#222222",
                       size = 7.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.35)),
                                breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3),
                                labels = short_number) +
    ggplot2::ylab("Set size")

  args <- list(
    d,
    intersect             = present,
    name                  = "",
    n_intersections       = max_intersections,
    min_degree            = if (show_empty) 0 else 1,
    sort_intersections_by = "cardinality",
    base_annotations      = list(Transcripts = size_layer),
    set_sizes             = set_size_layer,
    # ComplexUpset builds a theme per component rather than inheriting the one set
    # by theme_set(), so the font has to be injected here or the matrix, the set
    # sizes and the intersection bars each fall back to the ggplot default.
    themes                = ComplexUpset::upset_default_themes(
                              text = ggplot2::element_text(family = "Source Sans 3",
                                                           size = 10)),
    width_ratio           = 0.25,
    # Smaller dots than the default 3: with nine sets the matrix rows crowded
    # into one another.
    matrix                = ComplexUpset::intersection_matrix(
                              geom    = ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2),
                              segment = ggplot2::geom_segment(linewidth = 0.5))
  )

  # guides = "over" puts the fill legend in the empty cell above the set sizes,
  # to the right of the intersection bars, instead of a column of its own beside
  # the whole figure. Older ComplexUpset releases lack the argument, so fall back
  # to a collected legend on the right there.
  p <- tryCatch(do.call(ComplexUpset::upset, c(args, list(guides = "over"))),
                error = function(e) {
                  do.call(ComplexUpset::upset, args) &
                    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "right")
                })
  # Smaller keys, and a gap between the bars and the legend beside them.
  p <- p & ggplot2::theme(legend.key.size = ggplot2::unit(0.7, "lines"),
                          legend.margin   = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 0, 14),
                          legend.text     = ggplot2::element_text(size = ggplot2::rel(0.9)))

  if (!is.null(title) || !is.null(subtitle)) {
    p <- p + patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
      theme = ggplot2::theme(
        plot.title    = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5)))
  }
  p
}

# --- Circos ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Genome-wide view of the same transcripts the chromosome lollipops count, drawn
# with circlize. Organism-agnostic by construction:
#
# * Sectors are the assembled chromosomes (is_assembled_chromosome) found in the
#   metadata -- nothing is looked up for a species.
# * A sector's length is the furthest transcript end observed on that chromosome,
#   across the annotated and novel tables together, so both circos plots share one
#   geometry and can be compared side by side. This is the transcribed extent, a
#   slight underestimate of the chromosome itself.
# * A sector smaller than `min_frac` of the genome (a mitochondrion, a dot
#   chromosome) is enlarged to that size so it stays visible, and its label is
#   starred. Positions inside it are rescaled to match.
# * No cytoband: that is species-specific and most organisms have none.

# A CSV that is missing, unreadable or empty reads as NULL, so an optional input
# never stops the render.
read_csv_safe <- function(path) {
  if (is.null(path) || !file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  df <- tryCatch(read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(df) || !nrow(df)) NULL else df
}

# First candidate column present in `df`, or NA.
pick_col <- function(df, candidates) {
  hit <- intersect(candidates, names(df))
  if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_character_
}

# One row per transcript on an assembled chromosome: chromosome, start, end,
# strand (+ or -), group. NULL when the coordinate columns are absent.
circos_features <- function(df, chrom, group,
                            start_cols  = c("transcript_start", "start", "start_position"),
                            end_cols    = c("transcript_end", "end", "end_position"),
                            strand_cols = c("strand", "transcript_strand")) {
  if (is.null(df) || !nrow(df)) return(NULL)
  s  <- pick_col(df, start_cols)
  e  <- pick_col(df, end_cols)
  st <- pick_col(df, strand_cols)
  if (anyNA(c(s, e, st)) || !chrom %in% names(df)) return(NULL)

  strand <- as.character(df[[st]])
  strand[strand %in% c("1", "+1")] <- "+"
  strand[strand == "-1"]           <- "-"

  out <- data.frame(chromosome = as.character(df[[chrom]]),
                    start      = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(df[[s]])),
                    end        = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(df[[e]])),
                    strand     = strand,
                    group      = as.character(df[[group]]),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  out[is_assembled_chromosome(out$chromosome) & !is.na(out$start) & !is.na(out$end), ,
      drop = FALSE]
}

circos_sectors <- function(feat, min_frac = 0.012) {
  if (is.null(feat) || !nrow(feat)) return(NULL)
  ext <- stats::aggregate(end ~ chromosome, data = feat, FUN = max)
  names(ext)[2] <- "len"
  ext <- ext[order(order_chromosomes(ext$chromosome)), , drop = FALSE]

  floor_len       <- min_frac * sum(ext$len)
  ext$display_len <- pmax(ext$len, floor_len)
  ext$scale       <- ext$display_len / ext$len
  ext$enlarged    <- ext$display_len > ext$len
  ext$label       <- sub("^chr", "", ext$chromosome, ignore.case = TRUE)
  ext$label[ext$enlarged] <- paste0(ext$label[ext$enlarged], "*")
  rownames(ext) <- NULL
  ext
}

# Opens the circos canvas: a gap at 12 o'clock for the strand labels, then a label
# track and a plain ideogram track.
circos_start <- function(sectors, gap_top = 22) {
  n <- nrow(sectors)
  circlize::circos.clear()
  circlize::circos.par(start.degree = 90 - gap_top / 2,
                       gap.degree   = c(rep(1, max(n - 1, 0)), gap_top),
                       cell.padding = c(0, 0, 0, 0),
                       track.margin = c(0.004, 0.004),
                       points.overflow.warning = FALSE)
  circlize::circos.initialize(factor(sectors$chromosome, levels = sectors$chromosome),
                              xlim = cbind(0, sectors$display_len))

  labels <- setNames(sectors$label, sectors$chromosome)
  circlize::circos.track(ylim = c(0, 1), track.height = 0.05, bg.border = NA,
    panel.fun = function(x, y) {
      chr <- circlize::get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
      circlize::circos.text(circlize::get.cell.meta.data("xcenter"), 0.15, labels[[chr]],
                            facing = "bending.inside", niceFacing = TRUE,
                            adj = c(0.5, 0), cex = 0.68)
    })
  circlize::circos.track(ylim = c(0, 1), track.height = 0.02, bg.border = NA,
    panel.fun = function(x, y) {
      xl <- circlize::get.cell.meta.data("xlim")
      circlize::circos.rect(xl[1], 0, xl[2], 1, col = "#d9d9d9",
                            border = "#4d4d4d", lwd = 0.5)
    })
}

# Radius of the middle of the track just drawn, for the strand labels.
circos_track_mid <- function(sectors) {
  ti <- circlize::get.current.track.index()
  sx <- sectors$chromosome[1]
  mean(c(circlize::get.cell.meta.data("cell.top.radius",    sector.index = sx, track.index = ti),
         circlize::get.cell.meta.data("cell.bottom.radius", sector.index = sx, track.index = ti)))
}

# Alternating shading behind the lanes of a track, so each lane reads as a band.
circos_lane_background <- function(L) {
  xl <- circlize::get.cell.meta.data("xlim")
  circlize::circos.rect(rep(xl[1], L), 0:(L - 1), rep(xl[2], L), 1:L,
                        col = rep(c("#f5f4f1", "#ebe9e4"), length.out = L), border = NA)
}

# Per-bin counts for the annotated circos, one lane per group (first lane
# outermost). Bar height is scaled to the lane's own peak across both strands:
# protein-coding outnumbers small RNAs by orders of magnitude, so on a shared
# scale every lane but one would be flat. The peak is reported in the legend.
circos_lane_bins <- function(feat, sectors, bin_size, lanes) {
  L <- length(lanes)
  f <- merge(feat, sectors[, c("chromosome", "len", "scale")], by = "chromosome")
  f <- f[f$group %in% lanes, , drop = FALSE]
  f$bin <- floor(((f$start + f$end) / 2) / bin_size)
  b <- dplyr::count(f, strand, chromosome, bin, group, len, scale, name = "n")
  peak <- tapply(b$n, b$group, max)
  b %>%
    dplyr::mutate(peak = as.numeric(peak[group]),
                  base = L - match(group, lanes),
                  y0   = base + 0.08,
                  y1   = base + 0.08 + 0.84 * n / peak,
                  x0   = bin * bin_size * scale,
                  x1   = pmin((bin + 1) * bin_size, len) * scale)
}

# One strand of annotated transcripts: a histogram per lane.
circos_bin_track <- function(bins, colours, lanes, height = 0.2) {
  L <- length(lanes)
  circlize::circos.track(ylim = c(0, L), track.height = height, bg.border = NA,
    panel.fun = function(x, y) {
      circos_lane_background(L)
      chr <- circlize::get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
      b   <- bins[bins$chromosome == chr, , drop = FALSE]
      if (nrow(b)) {
        circlize::circos.rect(b$x0, b$y0, b$x1, b$y1,
                              col = unname(colours[as.character(b$group)]), border = NA)
      }
    })
}

# One strand of novel transcripts: one tick per transcript, one lane per category
# so a rare category is never hidden under a common one.
circos_tick_track <- function(feat, sectors, colours, lanes, height = 0.13) {
  L <- length(lanes)
  f <- merge(feat, sectors[, c("chromosome", "scale")], by = "chromosome")
  f$x    <- ((f$start + f$end) / 2) * f$scale
  f$lane <- L - match(f$group, lanes)          # first lane outermost
  circlize::circos.track(ylim = c(0, L), track.height = height, bg.border = NA,
    panel.fun = function(x, y) {
      circos_lane_background(L)
      chr <- circlize::get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
      g <- f[f$chromosome == chr & !is.na(f$lane), , drop = FALSE]
      if (nrow(g)) {
        circlize::circos.segments(g$x, g$lane + 0.06, g$x, g$lane + 0.94,
                                  col = unname(colours[g$group]), lwd = 1.1)
      }
    })
}

# Legend drawn inside the empty centre of the circle, so the figure is a square
# with no side column of white space. Header, entries and an optional note are
# stacked and centred on (0, 0).
circos_centre_legend <- function(header, labels, colours, type = c("fill", "line"),
                                 note = NULL, cex = 0.56) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  lg <- list(legend = labels, bty = "n", cex = cex, y.intersp = 1.15,
             xjust = 0.5, yjust = 1)
  lg <- if (type == "fill") c(lg, list(fill = colours, border = NA))
        else c(lg, list(col = colours, lwd = 3, lty = 1, seg.len = 1.2))

  size   <- do.call(legend, c(list(x = 0, y = 0, plot = FALSE), lg))
  gap    <- strheight("M", cex = cex) * 0.9
  h_head <- strheight(header, cex = cex * 1.1, font = 2)
  h_note <- if (is.null(note)) 0 else strheight(note, cex = cex * 0.9) + gap
  top    <- (h_head + gap + size$rect$h + h_note) / 2

  text(0, top, header, adj = c(0.5, 1), cex = cex * 1.1, font = 2)
  do.call(legend, c(list(x = 0, y = top - h_head - gap), lg))
  if (!is.null(note)) {
    text(0, top - h_head - gap - size$rect$h - gap, note,
         adj = c(0.5, 1), cex = cex * 0.9, col = "#555555")
  }
}

# Only what the reader cannot get from the caption: the lane order is stated
# there, so the centre keeps its space for the legend itself.
circos_note <- function(sectors, n_unstranded) {
  note <- character(0)
  if (any(sectors$enlarged)) note <- c(note, "* enlarged, not to scale")
  if (n_unstranded > 0) {
    note <- c(note, sprintf("%s unstranded not drawn", scales::comma(n_unstranded)))
  }
  if (length(note)) paste(note, collapse = "\n") else NULL
}

circos_strand_labels <- function(r_plus, r_minus) {
  # Just the sign: the gap at the top is narrow and "+"/"−" is read at a glance.
  text(0, r_plus,  "+",      font = 2, cex = 0.95)
  text(0, r_minus, "−", font = 2, cex = 0.95)
}

# Annotated transcripts: one lane per biotype, transcripts per bin as a histogram,
# + strand outside and - strand inside. `counts` is the legend total per biotype,
# taken from the lollipop table so the two figures state the same numbers.
draw_circos_annotated <- function(feat, sectors, colours, counts, bin_size = 1e6) {
  stranded     <- feat[feat$strand %in% c("+", "-"), , drop = FALSE]
  n_unstranded <- nrow(feat) - nrow(stranded)
  lanes <- names(colours)
  bins  <- circos_lane_bins(stranded, sectors, bin_size, lanes)
  peaks <- tapply(bins$n, as.character(bins$group), max)
  bin_label <- if (bin_size >= 1e6) sprintf("%s Mb", signif(bin_size / 1e6, 3))
               else sprintf("%s kb", signif(bin_size / 1e3, 3))
  # Thicker lanes than the novel plot's: 1 Mb bins are narrow, and the colour of
  # each lane only reads when the bars have height to show it.
  height <- min(0.3, 0.06 * length(lanes))

  par(mar = rep(0.1, 4), family = "Source Sans 3")
  circos_start(sectors)
  circos_bin_track(bins[bins$strand == "+", ], colours, lanes, height = height)
  r_plus  <- circos_track_mid(sectors)
  circos_bin_track(bins[bins$strand == "-", ], colours, lanes, height = height)
  r_minus <- circos_track_mid(sectors)
  circos_strand_labels(r_plus, r_minus)
  circos_centre_legend(
    sprintf("Annotated transcripts\n(peak per %s bin)", bin_label), cex = 0.5,
    sprintf("%s: %s (%s)", lanes, scales::comma(unname(counts[lanes])),
            scales::comma(unname(peaks[lanes]))),
    unname(colours), type = "fill",
    note = circos_note(sectors, n_unstranded))
  circlize::circos.clear()
}

# Novel transcripts: one tick per transcript, one lane per category, + strand
# outside and - strand inside.
draw_circos_novel <- function(feat, sectors, colours, counts) {
  stranded     <- feat[feat$strand %in% c("+", "-"), , drop = FALSE]
  n_unstranded <- nrow(feat) - nrow(stranded)
  lanes  <- names(colours)
  height <- min(0.27, 0.085 * length(lanes))

  par(mar = rep(0.1, 4), family = "Source Sans 3")
  circos_start(sectors)
  circos_tick_track(stranded[stranded$strand == "+", ], sectors, colours, lanes, height)
  r_plus  <- circos_track_mid(sectors)
  circos_tick_track(stranded[stranded$strand == "-", ], sectors, colours, lanes, height)
  r_minus <- circos_track_mid(sectors)
  circos_strand_labels(r_plus, r_minus)
  circos_centre_legend(
    "Novel transcripts\n(one tick = one transcript)",
    sprintf("%s: %s", lanes, scales::comma(unname(counts[lanes]))),
    unname(colours), type = "line",
    note = circos_note(sectors, n_unstranded))
  circlize::circos.clear()
}

# --- Feature counts (Assembly Statistics, panel A) ----------------------------
# Total / annotated / novel as separate facets with their own axis: novel features
# are a fraction of a percent of the total, so on a shared axis their bar is a
# sliver. Each count is printed beside its bar.
plot_feature_counts <- function(df, title = NULL) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = Count, y = Feature)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = Status), width = 0.65, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(Count)), hjust = -0.12, size = 8 / .pt) +
    facet_wrap(~Status, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = STATUS_COLOURS) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.42)),
                       breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3), labels = short_number) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#ececec", linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.spacing.x    = unit(1.4, "lines"),
      plot.title         = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Features", y = NULL)
}
```

## Introduction

This report presents the analysis of a transcriptome assembled from long-read RNA sequencing data. The objective is to identify and characterize annotated and novel protein-coding and lncRNA transcripts.

The report is structured into six sections:

1.  **Assembly Statistics:** Summary metrics of the transcriptome assembly.
2.  **Sample-level Expression Clustering:** Assessment of sample relationships before and after curation.
3.  **Isoform Diversity per Gene:** Isoforms per reference gene, and the known genes that gained novel isoforms.
4.  **Reference Transcriptome:** Characterization of detected reference transcripts, including biotype distribution, transcript length, and exon structure.
5.  **Novel Isoforms:** Description of newly identified transcripts and their supporting evidence.
6.  **Genomic Context:** Visualization of transcript models and read coverage across representative genomic loci.

Report generated automatically with the `integrativebioinformatics/pulposeq` pipeline.

<details>

<summary>**Metadatasets curation** — how the assembly was curated and filtered</summary>

Following transcriptome assembly with **Bambu** [^1], the extended annotations and count matrices contained in the `BambuOutput` object were curated to generate a high-confidence set of genes and transcripts suitable for downstream analyses. The curation workflow comprised the following steps:

[^1]: Chen, Ying, et al. "Context-aware transcript quantification from long-read RNA-seq data with Bambu." Nature methods 20.8 (2023): 1187-1195. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-023-01908-w

1.  Genes and transcripts with zero counts across all samples were removed, yielding filtered quantification files stored in the `bambu_filter/` results directory.
2.  Novel transcript isoforms were compared against the reference annotation using **GffCompare** [^2] and assessed for coding potential using **CPC2** [^3]. Isoforms were subsequently classified according to their GffCompare class code, coding-potential prediction, and the biotype of the associated reference gene.
3.  Transcript structural features, including exon composition and transcript architecture, were characterized directly from the reference annotation and assembled GTF files using **rtracklayer** [^5].
4.  Annotation files (GFT) and count matrices were restricted to the curated transcript set, and transcript classification and biotype information were incorporated into the final annotations.
5.  Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and expression heatmaps of Bambu were regenerated using the curated transcriptome, enabling direct comparison with the corresponding results obtained from the initial assembly.
6.  Per-base coverage profiles were exported as BigWig tracks for each sample, and selected genomic loci were visualized alongside transcript models using **plotgardener** [^6].
7.  Finally, annotations, expression matrices, and transcript characterization metrics were consolidated into standardized metadata tables to facilitate downstream analyses. Summary statistics of the curated assembly are presented throughout the following sections of this report.

[^2]: Pertea, Geo, and Mihaela Pertea. "GFF utilities: GffRead and GffCompare." F1000Research 9 (2020): ISCB-Comm. https://doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.23297.1

[^3]: Kang, Yu-Jian, et al. "CPC2: a fast and accurate coding potential calculator based on sequence intrinsic features." Nucleic Acids Research 45.W1 (2017): W12-W16. https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkx428

[^5]: Lawrence, Michael, Robert Gentleman, and Vincent Carey. "rtracklayer: an R package for interfacing with genome browsers." Bioinformatics 25.14 (2009): 1841-1842. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btp328

[^6]: Kramer, Nicole E., et al. "Plotgardener: cultivating precise multi-panel figures in R." Bioinformatics 38.7 (2022): 2042-2045. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btac057

The final validated outputs are provided in the `bambu_validated`, `novel_transcripts`, and `ref_transcripts` directories. Per-sample coverage tracks are available in `coverage/` as BigWig files, while genomic context visualizations can be found in `genomic_context/`.

::: callout-note
## Filtering criteria

A novel transcript is carried forward only if it meets **all** of the following:

- **Length ≥ 500 nt:** the consensus lower bound for a long non-coding RNA, applied to every category so the three stay comparable to one another.
- **A declared strand** (`+` or `-`): models Bambu could not orient are removed.
- **Non-zero counts** in at least one sample.
- **An accepted gffcompare class code:** `u`, `i`, `x`, `j`, `k`, `o`, `y`, `m` or `n`.

Nothing is filtered on structural evidence. Candidates carrying warning signs are reported with those signs attached, in [Tracking Evidence].
:::

  [Tracking Evidence]: #tracking-evidence

</details>

<details>

<summary>**gffcompare class codes** — what each code means</summary>

| Code | Description |
|:--------------------------------|:--------------------------------------|
| `u` | Unknown or intergenic |
| `i` | Fully contained within a reference intron (sub-classified as: *sense intronic* or *antisense* *intronic)* |
| `x` | Exonic overlap on the opposite strand (*antisense*) |
| `j` | Multi-exon transcript with at least one splice junction matching reference |
| `k` | Containment of reference transcript |
| `o` | Exonic overlap on the same strand |
| `y` | Contains reference within its introns |
| `m` | Retained intron(s), all introns matched or retained |
| `n` | Retained intron(s), not all introns matched or retained |

Class codes are reported exactly as gffcompare assigns them; pulposeq never recomputes or overrides one.

</details>

<details>

<summary>**How novel models are routed** — the three categories and the rules behind them</summary>

Each admitted model is assigned one of **three categories**, and those categories are the grouping used throughout this report.

**`u`, `i` and `x` share no splice structure with a reference.** `u` has no reference at all, `i` lies wholly inside an intron, and `x` overlaps on the opposite strand. The coding prediction stands on its own here, so it decides alone:

| Prediction | Category                     |
|:-----------|:-----------------------------|
| non-coding | **novel lncRNA candidate**   |
| coding     | **predicted protein-coding** |

A sense-intronic or antisense lncRNA sitting inside a protein-coding locus is still an lncRNA, and both Ensembl and GENCODE annotate them that way.

**`j`, `k`, `o`, `y`, `m` and `n` do share structure with a reference transcript.** A non-coding call carries less weight here: an unproductive isoform of a protein-coding gene — a retained intron, an NMD target, a truncated model — is predicted non-coding too, and calling one a novel lncRNA would assert a new non-coding gene at a locus that already has a coding one. So the reference gene's biotype is taken into account:

| Prediction | Reference gene | Category                     |
|:-----------|:---------------|:-----------------------------|
| coding     | any            | **predicted protein-coding** |
| non-coding | lncRNA         | **novel lncRNA candidate**   |
| non-coding | anything else  | **predicted non-coding**     |

**Predicted non-coding** says a model has no coding potential without asserting what it is, which is as much as the evidence supports for a non-coding isoform of a coding gene.

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong>Sense and antisense intronic transcripts</strong> — why transcript orientation is reported separately</summary>

Class code `i` ("fully contained within a reference intron") includes transcripts located entirely within a host intron regardless of strand orientation. Because these represent biologically distinct scenarios, pulposeq further classifies them as **sense** or **antisense** relative to the host gene. This strand-specific qualifier is an addition introduced by pulposeq and is not part of the original GffCompare classification.

A transcript located within an intron on the **same strand** as its host gene may correspond either to an independently transcribed unit or to a fragment of the host's unspliced precursor RNA. Genomic position alone cannot distinguish between these possibilities.

In contrast, an **antisense intronic transcript** originates from the opposite strand and therefore cannot be generated from the host gene's precursor transcript. As a result, its interpretation is generally less ambiguous.

This consideration is independent of coding potential and applies to any spliced host gene, including both protein-coding and lncRNA loci. Consequently, sense-intronic transcripts are retained rather than filtered during curation.

The classification is tracked throughout the report and summarized in the **Tracking Evidence** section. For transcripts selected for visualization, the **Genomic Context** section displays the complete host intron and corresponding coverage profiles, allowing readers to assess whether the observed signal is consistent with an independent transcript or with transcription from the host precursor RNA.

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong>pulposeq follows current consensus recommendations for lncRNA classification</strong></summary>

The structural and transcriptional complexity of eukaryotic genomes makes lncRNA classification challenging. Long non-coding transcripts may occur in intergenic, intronic, antisense, or overlapping genomic contexts and can originate from loci associated with diverse annotated gene biotypes, including protein-coding genes, pseudogenes, and other non-coding transcripts. Consequently, assigning transcript identity solely on the basis of the host locus biotype may overlook important features of the transcript itself.

To address this limitation, pulposeq implements a dual-layer classification strategy for novel transcript isoforms. Rather than inheriting the annotation of the parent locus, each novel transcript is evaluated independently based on:

1.  **Coding potential predictions**.
2.  **Structural characteristics**, including transcript length, exon-intron architecture, and its relationship to reference transcript models.

As a result, a transcript lacking coding potential is classified as a **novel lncRNA** even when it originates from a previously annotated protein-coding locus or another gene biotype. This approach distinguishes locus annotation from transcript identity and enables a more accurate representation of transcriptional complexity.

The classification framework follows current recommendations proposed by Mattick and colleagues [^7] for the annotation and nomenclature of lncRNAs.

[^7]: Mattick, J.S., Amaral, P.P., Carninci, P. et al. Long non-coding RNAs: definitions, functions, challenges and recommendations. Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol 24, 430–447 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41580-022-00566-8

#### Why the report says *candidate*

A transcript labelled a **novel lncRNA candidate** satisfies the filtering criteria above, is predicted non-coding, and either carries a class code that shares no structure with a reference (`u`, `i`, `x`) or shares structure with a reference gene that is itself an lncRNA. That is a well-defined set, and it is the set this report counts.

It is not a set of validated lncRNAs. A coding-potential prediction is evidence about sequence composition, not about whether a transcript is an independent transcriptional unit. Two situations need evidence the prediction cannot supply:

- A **sense-intronic** model cannot be distinguished from a fragment of its host's unspliced precursor by position alone.
- A model **sharing splice structure with a protein-coding gene** may be an unproductive isoform of that gene rather than a new non-coding locus; these are reported as *predicted non-coding* rather than as lncRNA candidates.

The [Tracking Evidence] section reports what other evidence each candidate carries. Nothing is filtered on that basis: a candidate set with the evidence stated per member is a stronger result than an unqualified count.

  [Tracking Evidence]: #tracking-evidence

#### Why the report uses the term *candidate*

A transcript classified as a **novel lncRNA candidate** has passed all filtering criteria, is predicted to lack coding potential, and either:

- belongs to a class code that does not share exon-intron structure with any reference transcript (`u`, `i`, or `x`); or
- is associated with a reference gene that is itself annotated as an lncRNA.

These transcripts constitute the candidate set reported throughout this document.

Importantly, candidate status should not be interpreted as definitive validation. Coding-potential prediction provides evidence regarding the likelihood that a transcript encodes a protein, but it does not establish whether the transcript represents an independent transcriptional unit.

Additional biological context may be required in several situations. For example:

- **Sense-intronic transcripts** may represent either independent transcripts or fragments of the host gene's unspliced precursor RNA.
- Transcripts **sharing splice structures with protein-coding genes** may correspond to unproductive or non-canonical isoforms of those genes rather than to distinct lncRNA loci. For this reason, such transcripts are reported as *predicted non-coding* rather than as lncRNA candidates.

The **Tracking Evidence** section summarizes the additional evidence available for each candidate transcript. These observations are reported to support interpretation and are not used as filtering criteria. Presenting the supporting evidence for every candidate provides a more informative and transparent view of the results than reporting candidate counts alone.

</details>

## Assembly Statistics

This section provides an overview of the curated transcriptome assembly at the gene and transcript levels. All statistics are derived from the curated Bambu output and summarize the features that were detected, quantified, and retained after the validation workflow.

Features are grouped into three categories:

- **Total** – All unique genes or transcripts identified in the assembly.
- **Annotated** – Features matching an existing reference annotation (Ensembl or GENCODE).
- **Novel** – Features discovered by Bambu that are not present in the reference annotation.

::: callout-warning
**Gene and transcript counts are not directly comparable.**

Bambu assigns read classes (RCs) that are incompatible with any known or assembled transcript to the gene level, allowing them to contribute to gene quantification. However, these incompatible RCs cannot be assigned to transcript isoforms and are therefore excluded from isoform-level quantification.

To ensure consistency between transcript characterization and expression analyses, the validation workflow retains only genes associated with compatible and successfully quantified transcript isoforms. As a result, the curated gene set represents the subset of genes supported by validated transcript models.
:::

```{r}
#| label: run-metrics
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

metrics <- tryCatch(read.csv(params$bambu_metrics, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
vsum    <- tryCatch(read.csv(params$validation_summary, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                    error = function(e) NULL)

get_metric <- function(k) {
  if (is.null(metrics)) return(NA_character_)
  v <- metrics$value[metrics$metric == k]
  if (length(v)) as.character(v[1]) else NA_character_
}

cat('::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}\n')
cat("## Run parameters and validation yield\n\n")

ndr <- get_metric("ndr_used")
cat(sprintf("**Novel discovery rate (NDR):** %s%s\n\n",
            ifelse(is.na(ndr), "not recorded", ndr),
            if (identical(get_metric("ndr_requested"), "auto"))
              " — selected automatically by Bambu" else " — set explicitly"))

if (!is.null(vsum)) {
  # Two decimals: 392,130 of 392,201 is 99.98%, and "100.0%" reads as a curation
  # that lost nothing at all.
  vtab <- data.frame(
    Feature            = vsum$feature_type,
    `Curated set`      = format(vsum$curated_set, big.mark = ","),
    `Total quantified` = format(vsum$total_quantified, big.mark = ","),
    `Recovery %`       = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * vsum$recovery),
    check.names        = FALSE
  )
  if (!is.null(vsum$extended_annotations)) {
    vtab$`Extended annotations` <- format(vsum$extended_annotations, big.mark = ",")
  }
  cat(knitr::kable(vtab, format = "markdown"), sep = "\n")
  cat(paste("\n\n**Total quantified** is the expressed set: features carrying at least",
            "one count in at least one sample, and the denominator recovery is measured",
            "against. **Extended annotation** is every feature Bambu quantified against,",
            "including those no read supports -- those are outside the curation and are",
            "not counted as losses.\n"))
}
cat("\n:::\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: get-overall-assembly-stats
#| include: false

# List bambu outputs to account for assembled and quantified genes/transcripts
bambu_outputs <- c(
  genes = params$counts_genes,
  transcripts = params$counts_transcript,
  fullLength = params$fl_counts_transcript,
  uniquelyMapped = params$u_counts_transcript
)

# Check if files exist
files_exist <- sapply(bambu_outputs, file.exists)
if (!all(files_exist)) {
  missing_files <- bambu_outputs[!files_exist]
  stop("Error: The following files were not found: ", paste(missing_files, collapse = ", "))
}

results_list <- list()
bambu_ids    <- list()
for (name in names(bambu_outputs)) {
  current_file <- bambu_outputs[[name]]
  tryCatch({
    data <- read.delim(current_file, header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
    id_column <- as.character(data[[1]])
    bambu_ids[[name]] <- id_column
    total_count <- nrow(data)
    annotated_count <- sum(!startsWith(id_column, "Bambu"))
    novel_count <- sum(startsWith(id_column, "Bambu"))
    file_result <- data.frame(Bambu = name, Total = total_count, Annotated = annotated_count, Novel = novel_count)
    results_list[[name]] <- file_result
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Warning: Could not process file '", basename(current_file), "' (named '", name, "'). Skipping.\n", sep = "")
    cat("Error message:", e$message, "\n")
  })
}

# Organize results
if (length(results_list) > 0) {
  bambu_df <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
  rownames(bambu_df) <- NULL
  bambu_df <- bambu_df %>%
    mutate(FeatureType = if_else(Bambu == "genes", "Gene", "Transcript")) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(Total, Annotated, Novel), names_to = "Status", values_to = "Count")
  write.csv(bambu_df, "Bambu_assembly_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("No files were successfully processed from the provided list.\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: prepare-to-plot-overall-assembly-stats
#| include: false

if (!exists("bambu_df")) {
  stop("Error: The data frame 'bambu_df' was not found.")
}
bambu_df$Status <- factor(bambu_df$Status, levels = c("Total", "Annotated", "Novel"))
bambu_df$Bambu <- factor(bambu_df$Bambu, levels = rev(c("genes", "transcripts", "fullLength", "uniquelyMapped")))

detected_tx <- unique(bambu_ids$transcripts)
tx_support  <- data.frame(
  transcript_id         = detected_tx,
  Status                = ifelse(startsWith(detected_tx, "Bambu"), "Novel", "Annotated"),
  `full-length support` = detected_tx %in% bambu_ids$fullLength,
  `unique support`      = detected_tx %in% bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped,
  check.names           = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors      = FALSE
)
```

::: callout-tip
## How to read panel B

Bambu writes three transcript count matrices, and the second two are subsets of the first:

- **Total**: every transcript with a non-zero estimated count.
- **Full-length support**: the transcript has reads spanning it end to end, from its start to its termination site.
- **Unique support**: the transcript has reads compatible with it and with no other isoform, so those reads are assigned to it directly rather than shared out.

A transcript can have both, one, or neither, so every transcript falls into exactly one of four combinations. Panel B shows the **share** of annotated and of novel transcripts in each combination. Proportions rather than counts, because the novel set is a fraction of a percent of the assembly and would not be visible on a shared count axis. Exact counts are in the table under the figure.

Support says how directly a transcript was measured; nothing is discarded on this basis. A transcript in *neither* was quantified only by expectation-maximisation, so its count is an inference from reads it shares with other isoforms.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-bambu-gene-transcript-stats
#| fig-cap: "**Summary of assembled genes and transcripts.** (A) Genes and transcripts detected by Bambu: total, annotated and novel, each panel on its own axis so the novel counts are readable. (B) Share of annotated and novel transcripts in each read-support combination. A transcript may have full-length support, unique support, both, or neither; *neither* marks transcripts quantified solely by expectation-maximisation from reads shared among compatible isoforms. Nearly all novel transcripts carry both forms of support, consistent with Bambu building novel isoforms from full-length read classes."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.5

# Bambu writes full-length and unique matrices only for transcripts, so panel B has
# no gene counterpart.
feature_counts <- bambu_df %>%
  filter(Bambu %in% c("genes", "transcripts")) %>%
  mutate(Feature = factor(if_else(Bambu == "genes", "Genes", "Transcripts"),
                          levels = c("Transcripts", "Genes")))

tx_support$Status <- factor(tx_support$Status, levels = c("Annotated", "Novel"))

plot_grid(
  plot_feature_counts(feature_counts, title = "Detected genes and transcripts"),
  plot_support_bars(tx_support, Status, title = "Read-level support of transcripts"),
  ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.95), labels = "AUTO", label_y = 1)
```

```{r}
#| label: support-status-counts
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

support_table(tx_support, Status, "Transcripts")
```

#### RNA biotypes

```{r}
#| label: get-lnc-pc-assembly-stats
#| include: false

# --- 1A. Check if Annotated Transcriptome Metadata exists ---
if (!file.exists(params$transcriptome_meta)) {
  stop("Error: The annotated transcriptome metadata file was not found at: ", params$transcriptome_meta)
}

# --- 1B. Check if Novel lncRNA/PC Metadata exists ---
if (!file.exists(params$novel_transcriptome_meta)) {
  stop("Error: The novel transcript metadata file was not found at: ", params$novel_transcriptome_meta)
}

# --- 2A. Import Annotated Transcriptome Metadata ---
tryCatch({
  ann_txome <- read.csv(params$transcriptome_meta)
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Critical Error reading annotated transcriptome metadata file: ", e$message)
})

# Collapse the older lncRNA vocabularies onto "lncRNA" once, here, so every
# `gene_biotype == "lncRNA"` downstream is right for an archived annotation as well
# as a current one. Only gene_biotype: transcript_biotype is left as the annotation
# wrote it, since the figures that break lncRNA genes down by transcript biotype are
# there to show exactly that detail.
ann_txome$gene_biotype[ann_txome$gene_biotype %in% LNCRNA_REF_BIOTYPES] <- "lncRNA"

# --- 2B. Import Novel lncRNA/PC Metadata ---
tryCatch({
  novel_tx <- read.csv(params$novel_transcriptome_meta)
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Critical Error reading novel transcript metadata file: ", e$message)
})

# The three categories a novel model is routed into. Display labels are defined once
# here and reused throughout the report, so a category is named identically in every
# figure, table and caption.
NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS <- c(
  novel_lncRNA         = "novel lncRNA candidate",
  novel_protein_coding = "predicted protein-coding",
  novel_non_coding     = "predicted non-coding"
)

# Read from pulposeq_transcript_biotype, never re-derived from the coding prediction.
# The prediction on its own cannot separate a novel lncRNA candidate from a predicted
# non-coding model -- both are called non-coding, and what distinguishes them is the
# biotype of the gene the model was compared against.
if (!"pulposeq_transcript_biotype" %in% names(novel_tx)) {
  stop("`pulposeq_transcript_biotype` is missing from ", params$novel_transcriptome_meta,
       ". The report cannot assign novel categories without it, and the coding ",
       "prediction is not a substitute.", call. = FALSE)
}

novel_tx$biotype <- unname(NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS[novel_tx$pulposeq_transcript_biotype])
novel_tx$biotype[is.na(novel_tx$biotype)] <- "novel (unclassified)"

# Display order of the routed categories, used for facet columns throughout.
novel_levels <- function(x) {
  lv <- c(unname(NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS), "novel (unclassified)")
  droplevels(factor(x, levels = c(lv, setdiff(sort(unique(as.character(x))), lv))))
}

raw_nov_pc_tx  <- unique(novel_tx$qry_id[novel_tx$biotype == "predicted protein-coding"])
raw_nov_lnc_tx <- unique(novel_tx$qry_id[novel_tx$biotype == "novel lncRNA candidate"])
raw_nov_nc_tx  <- unique(novel_tx$qry_id[novel_tx$biotype == "predicted non-coding"])

# --- 3. Bambu identifiers ---
# `bambu_ids` was populated in get-overall-assembly-stats, from the same read that
# counted the matrices. These files run to hundreds of thousands of rows on a full
# annotation, so they are read once.

# Identify if annotated transcript IDs contain versioning suffix
if (any(grepl("\\.", bambu_ids$transcripts))) {
```
