  version_suffix <- TRUE
} else {
  version_suffix <- FALSE
}

# --- 4. Extract ID vectors for each category (Transcripts Only) ---
ids <- list(
  # Protein-coding
  ann_pc_tx = if (version_suffix) {
    unique(ann_txome$transcript_id_version[ann_txome$gene_biotype == "protein_coding"])
  } else {
    unique(ann_txome$transcript_id[ann_txome$gene_biotype == "protein_coding"])
  },
  
  # lncRNAs
  ann_lnc_tx = if (version_suffix) {
    unique(ann_txome$transcript_id_version[ann_txome$gene_biotype == "lncRNA"])
  } else {
    unique(ann_txome$transcript_id[ann_txome$gene_biotype == "lncRNA"])
  },

  # Filter to only include true novel protein-coding features (starting with "Bambu")
  nov_pc_tx = raw_nov_pc_tx[startsWith(raw_nov_pc_tx, "Bambu")],

  # Filter to only include true novel lncRNA features (starting with "Bambu")
  nov_lnc_tx = raw_nov_lnc_tx[startsWith(raw_nov_lnc_tx, "Bambu")],

  # Intron-retention events are a third category, not a subset of either of the
  # above -- omitting them here would drop them from every summary below.
  nov_nc_tx = raw_nov_nc_tx[startsWith(raw_nov_nc_tx, "Bambu")]
)

# Helper function to count overlaps between Bambu outputs and our target IDs
count_overlap <- function(bambu_set, target_ids) {
  if (is.null(bambu_set) || length(bambu_set) == 0) return(0)
  sum(bambu_set %in% target_ids)
}

# --- 5. Quantify across categories ---
results_biotype <- list()

BIOTYPE_LABELS <- c(pc = "Protein-coding", lnc = "lncRNA", nc = "Non-coding")

for (bt in names(BIOTYPE_LABELS)) {
  biotype_label <- unname(BIOTYPE_LABELS[bt])

  # Transcript Level (Check all three transcript files)
  for (tx_cat in c("transcripts", "fullLength", "uniquelyMapped")) {
    # Intron retention exists only as a novel category -- there is no annotated
    # counterpart to look up, so ann_pc/ann_lnc have no ann_ir sibling.
    ann_t <- count_overlap(bambu_ids[[tx_cat]], ids[[paste0("ann_", bt, "_tx")]])
    nov_t <- count_overlap(bambu_ids[[tx_cat]], ids[[paste0("nov_", bt, "_tx")]])
    tot_t <- ann_t + nov_t
    
    results_biotype[[paste0(bt, "_", tx_cat)]] <- data.frame(
      FeatureType = "Transcript", Biotype = biotype_label, Bambu = tx_cat,
      Total = tot_t, Annotated = ann_t, Novel = nov_t
    )
  }
}

# --- 6. Organize and Save Results ---
if (length(results_biotype) > 0) {
  biotype_df <- do.call(rbind, results_biotype) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(Total, Annotated, Novel), names_to = "Status", values_to = "Count")

  # Ensure proper factor ordering
  biotype_df$Status <- factor(biotype_df$Status, levels = c("Total", "Annotated", "Novel"))
  biotype_df$Bambu <- factor(biotype_df$Bambu, levels = rev(c("transcripts", "fullLength", "uniquelyMapped")))

  write.csv(biotype_df, "Bambu_lncRNA_PC_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("No files were successfully processed to build the biotype summary.\n")
}
```

Bambu reports each transcript in three matrices: all assigned reads, reads spanning the transcript's full structure, and reads mapping to it uniquely. The three are **nested** — full-length and unique support are both subsets of total — so the informative question is not how many transcripts appear in each, but which transcripts appear in *both*.

A transcript with full-length **and** unique support is evidenced directly. One with neither was quantified entirely from expectation-maximisation over reads that never spanned it, and is the weakest thing in the assembly.

```{r}
#| label: support-sets-prep
#| include: false

# One row per detected transcript, with membership of the two support matrices as
# logical columns. Membership, not counts: this figure answers "which transcripts
# have which kinds of evidence", and the count distributions come later.
support_category <- c(
  ann_pc_tx  = "annotated protein-coding",
  ann_lnc_tx = "annotated lncRNA",
  nov_pc_tx  = "predicted protein-coding",
  nov_lnc_tx = "novel lncRNA candidate",
  nov_nc_tx  = "predicted non-coding"
)

detected <- unique(bambu_ids$transcripts)

cat_of <- rep(NA_character_, length(detected))
for (k in names(support_category)) {
  hit <- is.na(cat_of) & detected %in% ids[[k]]
  cat_of[hit] <- support_category[[k]]
}

support_sets <- data.frame(
  transcript_id            = detected,
  category                 = cat_of,
  `full-length support`    = detected %in% bambu_ids$fullLength,
  `unique support`         = detected %in% bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped,
  check.names              = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors         = FALSE
)

# Transcripts in the counts matrix that belong to none of the five categories are
# biotypes this figure does not track (small RNAs, pseudogenes and so on). Kept,
# and named, rather than silently dropped.
support_sets$category[is.na(support_sets$category)] <- "other biotypes"
support_sets$category <- factor(
  support_sets$category,
  levels = c("annotated protein-coding", "annotated lncRNA", "other biotypes",
             "predicted protein-coding", "novel lncRNA candidate", "predicted non-coding")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bambu-lnc-pc-stats
#| fig-cap: "**Read support for every transcript in the validated assembly, by category.** Share of each category's transcripts in each combination of full-length and unique support; the number of transcripts in the category is under its name. *Neither* (no full-length and no uniquely-mapping read) marks transcripts quantified purely from expectation-maximisation. Shares under 6% are not labelled; exact counts are in the table below."
#| fig-width: 4.8
#| fig-height: !expr bar_height(nlevels(droplevels(support_sets$category)))

plot_support_bars(
  support_sets, category,
  title = "Read-level support across biotypes")
```

```{r}
#| label: support-category-counts
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

support_table(support_sets, category, "Category")
```

## Sample-level Expression Clustering

Bambu generates principal component analysis (PCA) plots and expression heatmaps to summarize relationships among samples based on transcript expression profiles.

The figures below are presented in two versions:

- **Raw assembly** – generated directly from the initial Bambu assembly output.
- **Curated assembly** – generated after transcript validation, classification, and metadata refinement.

Comparing the two sets of figures highlights the extent to which transcript filtering and validation influence sample clustering patterns, providing a direct assessment of the contribution of discarded transcript models to the overall expression signal.

```{r}
#| label: plot-availability
#| include: false

plot_params <- list(
  raw_pca                 = params$raw_pca,
  raw_pca_grouped         = params$raw_pca_grouped,
  raw_heatmap_gene        = params$raw_heatmap_gene,
  raw_heatmap_transcript  = params$raw_heatmap_transcript,
  post_pca                = params$post_pca,
  post_pca_grouped        = params$post_pca_grouped,
  post_heatmap_gene       = params$post_heatmap_gene,
  post_heatmap_transcript = params$post_heatmap_transcript
)

# A plot is only embedded if the file is present and non-empty, so a stub run or
# a partially completed execution does not break the render.
plot_available <- vapply(plot_params, function(p) {
  !is.null(p) && file.exists(p) && file.info(p)$size > 0
}, logical(1))

# include_graphics must be handed a vector: called inside a loop it would not be
# auto-printed and nothing would be embedded.
show_plots <- function(keys) {
  paths <- unlist(plot_params[keys][plot_available[keys]], use.names = FALSE)
  if (length(paths) > 0) knitr::include_graphics(paths) else NULL
}
```

## Isoform Diversity per Gene

How many isoforms each reference gene carries in this assembly, and which known genes gained novel isoforms. Genes are grouped by their reference biotype: **protein-coding**, **lncRNA**, and **other** (every other gene biotype: pseudogenes, small RNAs and the rest).

A novel isoform is counted under the gene **Bambu assigned it to** (`qry_gene_id`), which is the gene it is an isoform *of*. This is deliberately not gffcompare's compared gene: for intronic (`i`) and antisense (`x`) models that is the gene they sit inside or run antisense to, not the gene they belong to. Novel isoforms placed in new Bambu genes have no reference gene and are not counted here.

```{r}
#| label: isoform-diversity-prep
#| include: false

HOST_LEVELS  <- c("protein-coding", "lncRNA", "other")
# Isoform Diversity section: turbo.
HOST_COLOURS <- setNames(TUR_FULL(3), HOST_LEVELS)

host_group <- function(bt) {
  bt <- as.character(bt)
  factor(dplyr::case_when(is.na(bt) | !nzchar(bt)            ~ NA_character_,
                          bt == "protein_coding"             ~ "protein-coding",
                          bt %in% c("lncRNA", LNCRNA_REF_BIOTYPES) ~ "lncRNA",
                          TRUE                               ~ "other"),
         levels = HOST_LEVELS)
}

# Every id form the reference uses (bare and versioned) mapped onto the bare
# gene id, so a novel isoform's gene matches whichever form Bambu wrote.
gene_lut <- c(setNames(ann_txome$gene_id, ann_txome$gene_id),
              if ("gene_id_version" %in% names(ann_txome))
                setNames(ann_txome$gene_id, ann_txome$gene_id_version))
gene_lut <- gene_lut[!duplicated(names(gene_lut))]

gene_label <- function(name, id) ifelse(is.na(name) | !nzchar(name), id, name)

# Annotated isoforms detected per gene.
ann_iso <- ann_txome %>%
  dplyr::distinct(gene_id, transcript_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gene_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(gene_name = dplyr::first(gene_name),
                   gene_biotype = dplyr::first(gene_biotype),
                   n_annotated = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

# Novel isoforms per known gene, from Bambu's gene assignment. Older metadata
# without the qry_ columns falls back to gffcompare's compared gene.
nov_gene_col <- pick_col(novel_tx, c("qry_gene_id", "compared_gene_id"))
nov_name_col <- pick_col(novel_tx, c("qry_gene_name", "compared_gene_name"))
nov_bt_col   <- pick_col(novel_tx, c("qry_gene_biotype", "compared_gene_biotype"))
uses_bambu_gene <- identical(nov_gene_col, "qry_gene_id")

novel_gene_tx <- NULL
n_novel_new_genes <- NA_integer_
if (!is.na(nov_gene_col)) {
  raw_id <- as.character(novel_tx[[nov_gene_col]])
  key    <- unname(gene_lut[raw_id])
  nov_bt <- if (is.na(nov_bt_col)) NA_character_ else as.character(novel_tx[[nov_bt_col]])
  # A reference gene with no detected annotated isoform is still a known gene:
  # its biotype comes from the novel metadata instead.
  known  <- !is.na(key) | (!is.na(nov_bt) & nzchar(nov_bt) & !is.na(raw_id) &
                             !startsWith(raw_id, "Bambu"))
  known[is.na(known)] <- FALSE
  key[is.na(key)] <- raw_id[is.na(key)]

  novel_gene_tx <- data.frame(
    qry_id    = novel_tx$qry_id,
    category  = novel_levels(novel_tx$biotype),
    gene_id   = key,
    gene_name = if (is.na(nov_name_col)) NA_character_ else as.character(novel_tx[[nov_name_col]]),
    gene_bt   = nov_bt,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[known, , drop = FALSE]
  n_novel_new_genes <- sum(!known)
}

nov_iso <- if (!is.null(novel_gene_tx) && nrow(novel_gene_tx)) {
  novel_gene_tx %>%
    dplyr::group_by(gene_id) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(gene_name_nov = dplyr::first(gene_name),
                     gene_bt_nov   = dplyr::first(gene_bt),
                     n_novel       = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")
} else {
  data.frame(gene_id = character(0), gene_name_nov = character(0),
             gene_bt_nov = character(0), n_novel = integer(0))
}

# All isoforms per reference gene: annotated plus novel.
gene_iso <- dplyr::full_join(ann_iso, nov_iso, by = "gene_id") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(n_annotated = dplyr::coalesce(n_annotated, 0L),
                n_novel     = dplyr::coalesce(n_novel, 0L),
                value       = n_annotated + n_novel,
                gene        = gene_label(dplyr::coalesce(gene_name, gene_name_nov), gene_id),
                .x          = host_group(dplyr::coalesce(gene_biotype, gene_bt_nov))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(.x), value > 0) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(.clr = .x)

top_iso    <- top_genes(gene_iso, n = 5)
has_iso    <- nrow(gene_iso) > 0

# Novel isoforms per known gene, split by the category of the novel isoform.
host_bt <- setNames(as.character(gene_iso$.x), gene_iso$gene_id)
host_nm <- setNames(gene_iso$gene, gene_iso$gene_id)
novel_host <- if (!is.null(novel_gene_tx) && nrow(novel_gene_tx)) {
  novel_gene_tx %>%
    dplyr::count(gene_id, category, name = "value") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(gene = unname(host_nm[gene_id]),
                  .x   = factor(unname(host_bt[gene_id]), levels = HOST_LEVELS),
                  .fac = category,
                  .clr = category) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.x))
} else NULL
has_novel_host <- !is.null(novel_host) && nrow(novel_host) > 0
h_novel_bins <- if (has_novel_host) {
  bar_height(nrow(dplyr::distinct(novel_host, .fac, .x)), base = 0.8, per = 0.3)
} else 3
top_novel_host <- if (has_novel_host) top_genes(novel_host, n = 5) else NULL

# Top-gene table: one row per group, the five names in one cell.
top_table <- function(top, group_names) {
  top %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(c(".fac", ".x")))) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      `Top 5 genes (isoforms)` = paste(label, collapse = ", "),
      Note = ifelse(dplyr::first(n_tied) > sum(value == dplyr::first(cutoff)),
                    sprintf("%d genes tie at %s; first by name shown",
                            dplyr::first(n_tied), dplyr::first(cutoff)), ""),
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    stats::setNames(c(group_names, "Top 5 genes (isoforms)", "Note"))
}
```

Genes are ranked from most to fewest isoforms, so the length of each curve is the number of genes. Diamonds mark the five genes with the most isoforms in each biotype, marked on the curve and listed with their counts in the panel corner, each name coloured like its curve. Both axes log10."
#| eval: !expr has_iso

plot_rank_curve(dplyr::mutate(gene_iso, .fac = .x), HOST_COLOURS,
                title = "Isoforms per reference gene", legend = FALSE)

```{r}
#| label: novel-isoforms-per-gene-note
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if (has_novel_host) {
  genes_tab <- novel_host %>%
    dplyr::count(.fac, .x, name = "genes") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = .x, values_from = genes, values_fill = 0)
  names(genes_tab)[1] <- "Novel isoform category"
  cat("**Known genes with at least one novel isoform**, by reference gene biotype:\n\n")
  cat(knitr::kable(genes_tab, format = "markdown"), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n\n<details><summary>Top 5 genes per category and biotype</summary>\n\n")
  cat(knitr::kable(top_table(top_novel_host, c("Novel isoform category", "Gene biotype")),
                   format = "markdown"), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n\n</details>\n\n")
}
if (!is.na(n_novel_new_genes) && n_novel_new_genes > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("%s novel isoforms belong to new Bambu genes and are not counted above.\n\n",
              scales::comma(n_novel_new_genes)))
}
if (!uses_bambu_gene) {
  cat("This metadata has no `qry_gene_id` column, so novel isoforms were counted under",
      "gffcompare's compared gene instead of Bambu's gene assignment.\n\n")
}
```

## Reference Transcriptome

In this section, we focus exclusively on the **annotated** portion of the transcriptome. These are transcripts that match known entries in public databases. By analyzing their biotypes, lengths, and exon structures, we can understand the composition of the known transcriptome in our samples and establish a baseline for comparison with novel transcripts.

### Biotypes

Biotypes classify RNAs based on their function or characteristics (e.g., `protein_coding`, `lncRNA`, `miRNA`).

```{r}
#| label: data-prep-annotated
#| include: false

# Load and prepare data
summary_data <- ann_txome %>% 
  group_by(gene_biotype, transcript_biotype) %>% 
  summarise(count = n_distinct(transcript_id_version), .groups = 'drop')

# Categorize biotypes
protein_coding <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype == "protein_coding")
lncRNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype == "lncRNA")
pseudogene_RNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(str_detect(gene_biotype, "pseudogene")) %>% mutate(category = "Pseudogene")
small_RNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype %in% c("snoRNA", "snRNA", "scaRNA", "sRNA", "rRNA", "misc_RNA", "miRNA"))
Tcell_RNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype %in% c("TR_V_gene", "TR_J_gene", "TR_D_gene", "TR_C_gene")) %>% mutate(category = "TCR elements")
IG_RNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype %in% c("IG_V_gene", "IG_J_gene", "IG_D_gene", "IG_C_gene")) %>% mutate(category = "Immunoglobulin elements")

# Gather all biotypes that have already been classified above
classified_biotypes <- unique(c(
  protein_coding$gene_biotype,
  lncRNAs$gene_biotype,
  pseudogene_RNAs$gene_biotype,
  small_RNAs$gene_biotype,
  Tcell_RNAs$gene_biotype,
  IG_RNAs$gene_biotype
))

other_RNAs_explicit <- summary_data %>%
  filter(!gene_biotype %in% classified_biotypes) %>%
  mutate(category = "all other biotypes")

biotype_groups <- drop_empty_groups(list(
  `Protein-coding`  = protein_coding,
  `lncRNA`          = lncRNAs,
  `Small RNAs`      = small_RNAs,
  `Pseudogenes`     = pseudogene_RNAs,
  `TCR elements`    = Tcell_RNAs,
  `IG elements`     = IG_RNAs,
  `Other biotypes`  = other_RNAs_explicit
))

create_plot <- function(data, title) {
  d <- data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(transcript_biotype) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(count = sum(count), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(.grp = "")

  plot_count_lollipop(d, x = transcript_biotype, y = .grp,
                      title = title,
                      x_lab = "Transcript biotype", count_lab = "Transcripts",
                      complete_grid = FALSE)
}

# Height per tab: one row per transcript biotype in the group.
biotype_tab_height <- vapply(biotype_groups, function(g)
  lollipop_height(dplyr::n_distinct(g$transcript_biotype), base = 1.3), numeric(1))

```

#### Transcript biotype diversity

Each tab holds one category group, with that group's transcript biotypes along the x axis and the exact transcript count printed above each point. Counts are summed across the gene biotypes in the group.

Only groups actually present in the supplied annotation get a tab.

```{r}
#| label: fig-biotype-groups
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
#| fig-cap: "Transcript Counts for Major RNA Categories. This panel shows the distribution of transcript biotypes within four main gene biotype categories: Protein-coding RNAs, Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), Small RNAs, and a consolidated group of all other RNA types."

tabs <- lapply(names(biotype_groups), function(nm) {
  knitr::knit_child(
    text = c(
      sprintf("##### %s", nm),
      "",
      "```{r}",
      "#| echo: false",
      "#| fig-width: 6",
      sprintf("#| fig-height: %.1f", biotype_tab_height[[nm]]),
      sprintf('create_plot(biotype_groups[["%s"]],', nm),
      sprintf('            "%s transcript biotypes")', nm),
      "```",
      ""
    ),
    envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE)
})

cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
cat(unlist(tabs), sep = "\n")
cat("\n:::\n\n")
```

#### Gene Biotype Diversity Across Chromosomes

This visualization shows the distribution of gene biotypes across chromosomes, highlighting differences in genomic organization and chromosome-specific enrichment patterns.

```{r}
#| label: prep-chr-data
#| include: false

# One row per annotated transcript with its biotype group and chromosome class.
# The lollipops count these rows and the circos plot draws them, so both figures
# are built from exactly the same transcripts.
ann_chr_tx <- ann_txome %>%
  mutate(biotype = case_when(
           str_detect(gene_biotype, "pseudogene")          ~ "pseudogene",
           gene_biotype %in% SMALL_RNA_BIOTYPES             ~ "small_RNA",
           gene_biotype %in% c("protein_coding", "lncRNA")  ~ gene_biotype,
           TRUE                                             ~ "other"),
         chromosome = chromosome_name,
         chr_class  = if_else(is_assembled_chromosome(chromosome), "assembled", "scaffold"))

chr_gb <- ann_chr_tx %>%
  count(chr_class, chromosome, biotype, name = "count")

# droplevels so a biotype absent from the data never reserves an empty panel column
chr_gb$biotype <- droplevels(factor(chr_gb$biotype,
  levels = c("protein_coding", "lncRNA", "small_RNA", "pseudogene", "other")))

chr_gb_asm <- chr_gb %>% filter(chr_class == "assembled") %>%
  mutate(chromosome = order_chromosomes(chromosome))
chr_gb_scf <- chr_gb %>% filter(chr_class == "scaffold") %>%
  mutate(chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = sort(unique(chromosome))))

has_scaffolds <- nrow(chr_gb_scf) > 0

h_chr_asm <- lollipop_height(nlevels(chr_gb_asm$chromosome), base = 1.3, per = 0.17)
h_chr_scf <- if (has_scaffolds) {
  lollipop_height(nlevels(chr_gb_scf$chromosome), base = 1.3, per = 0.17)
} else 3

# --- Circos inputs -------------------------------------------------------------
# Coordinates come from the metadata itself: transcript_start/transcript_end/strand
# for the reference, start/end/strand for the novel models. The sector geometry is
# derived from both tables together, so the annotated and novel circos plots share
# one layout. Nothing is species-specific.
circ_ann <- circos_features(ann_chr_tx, chrom = "chromosome", group = "biotype")
circ_nov <- circos_features(novel_tx,   chrom = "seqnames",   group = "biotype")
CIRCOS_SECTORS <- circos_sectors(rbind(circ_ann, circ_nov))

has_circos_ann <- !is.null(circ_ann) && nrow(circ_ann) > 0 && !is.null(CIRCOS_SECTORS)
has_circos_nov <- !is.null(circ_nov) && nrow(circ_nov) > 0 && !is.null(CIRCOS_SECTORS)
```

::: {.panel-tabset}
##### Assembled chromosomes

```{r}
#| label: fig-gb-across-chr
#| fig-cap: "**Chromosomal Distribution of Gene Biotypes.** Transcript isoforms of each biotype annotated on every assembled chromosome. One column per biotype, each with its own count axis (pseudo-log), and the exact count printed beside each point. A chromosome carrying none of a biotype sits on the baseline as a hollow point labelled 0."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: !expr h_chr_asm
#| column: page

plot_chr_distribution(
  chr_gb_asm,
  "Gene Biotype Diversity Across Chromosomes",
  "Transcript isoforms per biotype on each assembled chromosome",
  colours = ANN_BIOTYPE_COLOURS
)
```

##### Circos view

```{r}
#| label: fig-gb-circos
#| fig-cap: "**Genome-wide distribution of annotated transcripts.** The transcripts counted in the lollipop tab, positioned along each assembled chromosome. One lane per biotype, bars giving transcripts per 1 Mb bin, each lane scaled to its own peak (in brackets in the legend) so the rarer biotypes stay visible; lanes follow the legend order, outermost first. The + strand ring is outside, the − strand ring inside. Sector length is the furthest transcript end observed on that chromosome in this run, so no species-specific chromosome sizes are assumed; a starred sector was enlarged to stay visible."
#| fig-width: 5.5

#| eval: !expr has_circos_ann

ann_circ_counts <- tapply(chr_gb_asm$count, as.character(chr_gb_asm$biotype), sum)
draw_circos_annotated(
  circ_ann, CIRCOS_SECTORS,
  colours = palette_for(levels(chr_gb_asm$biotype), ANN_BIOTYPE_COLOURS),
  counts  = ann_circ_counts)
```

### Sequence Length

Here, we investigate the length of transcripts across different biotypes.

selected_tx <- ann_txome %>% filter(gene_biotype %in% c("protein_coding", "lncRNA", "miRNA", "snoRNA", "snRNA"))
selected_tx$gene_biotype <- factor(selected_tx$gene_biotype, levels = c("protein_coding", "lncRNA", "miRNA", "snoRNA", "snRNA"))
median_stx <- selected_tx %>% group_by(gene_biotype) %>% summarise(median_length = median(transcript_length), .groups = 'drop')

## Novel Isoforms

This section summarizes the characterization of transcripts that were not present in the reference annotation. Novel transcript models are grouped into three categories:

- **Novel lncRNA candidates**
- **Predicted protein-coding transcripts**
- **Predicted non-coding transcripts**

Unless otherwise stated, all counts reported in this section refer to **candidate transcripts**. These transcripts satisfy the classification criteria implemented by the pipeline but have not been experimentally validated as independent transcriptional units. Supporting evidence associated with each candidate is summarized in the [Tracking Evidence].

  [Tracking Evidence]: #tracking-evidence

> The metadata behind this section is `novel_transcripts_validated_metadata.csv`, which contains all classified novel transcript models.

> **About the Tools:**
>
> - **GFFRead** converts transcript annotations from GTF format into transcript sequences in FASTA format using the reference genome sequence.
> - **GFFCompare** compares assembled transcript models against a reference annotation and assigns a classification code describing their structural relationship to known transcripts (e.g. novel isoforms, intronic transcripts, or intergenic transcripts).
> - **CPC2** evaluates the coding potential of transcript sequences and classifies them as likely protein-coding or non-coding.

### Biotypes and Classification

```{r}
#| label: load-data-novel
#| include: false

class_counts <- novel_tx %>% group_by(biotype, classification) %>% summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop')

class_counts$biotype <- novel_levels(class_counts$biotype)
h_p20 <- lollipop_height(dplyr::n_distinct(class_counts$classification))

# One facet row per routed category.
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-novel-biotypes-and-classes
#| fig-cap: "**GFFCompare classification of the novel candidates.** Counts per classification, one column per routed category, each with its own count axis."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: !expr h_p20

p20 <- plot_count_lollipop(
  class_counts, x = classification, y = biotype,
  title = "GFFCompare classification of novel candidates",
  x_lab = "Classification", count_lab = "Transcripts", colours = NOVEL_COLOURS)
p20
```

#### Coding-potential features (CPC2)

CPC2 [^3] calls a transcript coding or non-coding from four features of its longest putative open reading frame (ORF), and those features are shown here per routed category:

- **Coding probability**: CPC2's output score; 0.5 or more is called coding. Categories are partly defined by this call, so it is drawn as a histogram that counts how many calls sit close to the cut-off rather than as a distribution to compare.
- **Peptide length**: length in amino acids of the peptide the longest ORF would encode.
- **Fickett score**: Fickett TESTCODE, a measure of the nucleotide-position bias typical of coding sequence; higher is more coding-like.
- **Isoelectric point (pI)**: of that putative peptide.
- **ORF integrity**: whether the longest ORF has both a start and a stop codon.

A non-coding call backed by a long, complete ORF and a coding-like Fickett score is weaker than one with a short or incomplete ORF, whatever the probability says.

```{r}
#| label: cpc2-prep
#| include: false

# The features come from the novel metadata. The validated table is used when it
# carries them; otherwise they are joined in from the full novel table by id.
CPC_COLS <- list(
  coding_prob    = c("coding_prob", "coding_probability"),
  peptide_length = c("peptide_length"),
  Fickett_score  = c("Fickett_score", "fickett_score"),
  pI             = c("pI", "pi", "isoelectric_point"),
  ORF_integrity  = c("ORF_integrity", "orf_integrity"))

cpc_source <- novel_tx
if (is.na(pick_col(cpc_source, CPC_COLS$peptide_length))) {
  all_meta <- read_csv_safe(params$novel_all_meta)
  if (!is.null(all_meta) && "qry_id" %in% names(all_meta)) {
    keep <- c("qry_id", unlist(lapply(CPC_COLS, function(cc) pick_col(all_meta, cc))))
    keep <- unique(keep[!is.na(keep)])
    cpc_source <- dplyr::left_join(
      novel_tx[, setdiff(names(novel_tx), setdiff(keep, "qry_id")), drop = FALSE],
      all_meta[, keep, drop = FALSE], by = "qry_id")
  }
}

cpc <- data.frame(qry_id = cpc_source$qry_id, category = novel_levels(cpc_source$biotype))
for (m in names(CPC_COLS)) {
  col <- pick_col(cpc_source, CPC_COLS[[m]])
  cpc[[m]] <- if (is.na(col)) NA_real_ else suppressWarnings(as.numeric(cpc_source[[col]]))
}

cpc_has <- vapply(names(CPC_COLS), function(m) any(!is.na(cpc[[m]])), logical(1))
has_cpc_metrics <- any(cpc_has[c("coding_prob", "peptide_length", "Fickett_score", "pI")])
has_cpc_orf     <- cpc_has[["ORF_integrity"]]

# One box-plot panel per feature, x = routed category.
plot_cpc_metric <- function(d, metric, title, y_lab, log = FALSE, cutoff = NULL) {
  d <- d[!is.na(d[[metric]]), , drop = FALSE]
  if (log) d <- d[d[[metric]] > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  d$value <- d[[metric]]
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = category, y = value, fill = category)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = NOVEL_COLOURS, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(12)) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(0.85), lineheight = 0.85),
          plot.title  = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = rel(1))) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = y_lab)
  if (!is.null(cutoff)) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = cutoff, linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.3,
                        colour = "#555555")
  }
  if (log) p + scale_y_log10_std() else p
}

# Coding probability is bounded to [0, 1] and piles up at the ends, where a
# violin's kernel is least accurate, and the categories were partly defined by
# it. A histogram strip per category shows the pile-up without smoothing and
# makes the borderline calls near the 0.5 cut-off countable; each row states the
# share of its transcripts within 0.1 of the cut-off.
plot_cpc_prob_hist <- function(d, title = "Coding probability", cutoff = 0.5, band = 0.1) {
  d <- d[!is.na(d$coding_prob), , drop = FALSE]
  near <- d %>%
    dplyr::group_by(category) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(lab = sprintf("%s within %.1f\u2013%.1f",
                                   scales::percent(mean(abs(coding_prob - cutoff) <= band),
                                                   accuracy = 0.1),
                                   cutoff - band, cutoff + band),
                     .groups = "drop")
  ggplot(d, aes(x = coding_prob, fill = category)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = cutoff - band, xmax = cutoff + band, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#f0f0f0") +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, boundary = 0, closed = "left", colour = NA) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = cutoff, linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "#555555") +
    geom_text(data = near, aes(x = 1, y = Inf, label = lab), hjust = 1, vjust = 1.4,
              size = 5.8 / .pt, colour = "#333333", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = NOVEL_COLOURS, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                       labels = c("0", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "1"),
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.35)),
                       breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 2), labels = short_number) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(category), scales = "free_y",
               labeller = labeller(category = label_wrap_gen(12))) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
          panel.spacing.y    = unit(0.25, "lines"),
          strip.text.y       = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, size = rel(0.8)),
          axis.text.y        = element_text(size = rel(0.75)),
          plot.title         = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = rel(1))) +
    labs(title = title, x = "CPC2 coding probability", y = "Transcripts")
}

ORF_LEVELS <- c("complete ORF", "incomplete ORF")
cpc_orf <- if (has_cpc_orf) {
  cpc %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(ORF_integrity)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(orf = factor(ifelse(ORF_integrity > 0, ORF_LEVELS[1], ORF_LEVELS[2]),
                               levels = ORF_LEVELS)) %>%
    dplyr::count(category, orf, name = "n") %>%
    tidyr::complete(category, orf, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(category) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(n_grp = sum(n), frac = ifelse(n_grp > 0, n / n_grp, 0)) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::filter(n_grp > 0)
} else NULL
# Chunk options are evaluated even when the chunk is skipped, so the height is
# computed here, where a missing table cannot break it.
h_cpc_orf <- if (has_cpc_orf) bar_height(nlevels(droplevels(cpc_orf$category))) else 2
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-cpc2-metrics
#| fig-cap: "**CPC2 coding-potential features by routed category.** (A) Histogram of CPC2's coding probability per category, in bins of 0.05; the dashed line is the 0.5 cut-off and the grey band 0.4–0.6, and each row states the share of its transcripts inside that band, the calls closest to going the other way. (B–D) Box plots of the length of the peptide encoded by the longest ORF (log10; transcripts with no ORF are left out), the Fickett TESTCODE score and the isoelectric point of that peptide."
#| eval: !expr has_cpc_metrics
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 5.4

cpc_panels <- list(
  if (cpc_has[["coding_prob"]]) plot_cpc_prob_hist(cpc),
  if (cpc_has[["peptide_length"]])
    plot_cpc_metric(cpc, "peptide_length", "Peptide length", "Amino acids (log10)", log = TRUE),
  if (cpc_has[["Fickett_score"]])
    plot_cpc_metric(cpc, "Fickett_score", "Fickett score", "Fickett TESTCODE"),
  if (cpc_has[["pI"]])
    plot_cpc_metric(cpc, "pI", "Isoelectric point", "pI"))
cpc_panels <- Filter(Negate(is.null), cpc_panels)

plot_grid(plotlist = cpc_panels, ncol = 2, labels = "AUTO", label_size = 11)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-cpc2-orf
#| fig-cap: "**ORF integrity by routed category.** Share of each category whose longest ORF has both a start and a stop codon (*complete*) or lacks one of them (*incomplete*), as CPC2 reports it. Shares under 10% are not labelled."
#| eval: !expr has_cpc_orf
#| fig-width: 4.8
#| fig-height: !expr h_cpc_orf

cpc_orf$.lab <- factor(sprintf("%s\n(n = %s)",
                               vapply(as.character(cpc_orf$category), function(z)
                                 paste(strwrap(z, 20), collapse = "\n"), character(1)),
                               scales::comma(cpc_orf$n_grp)))
cpc_orf$.lab <- factor(cpc_orf$.lab, levels = rev(unique(cpc_orf$.lab[order(cpc_orf$category)])))

ggplot(cpc_orf, aes(x = frac, y = .lab, fill = orf)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.78, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(frac >= 0.1, scales::percent(frac, accuracy = 1), ""),
                colour = orf),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
            size = 6.5 / .pt, show.legend = FALSE) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c("white", "#222222"), ORF_LEVELS), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = c("0", "", "50%", "", "100%"), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(0.85), lineheight = 0.9),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#ececec", linewidth = 0.3),

  med <- function(v) if (all(is.na(v))) "" else format(round(stats::median(v, na.rm = TRUE), 2), big.mark = ",")
  tab <- cpc %>%

      "the novel metadata for this run, so this subsection has no figures.\n\n")

#### What each novel call was compared against

Every novel model except the intergenic ones (`u`) was compared against a reference transcript by gffcompare. The match is recorded at both the gene and the transcript level, and where they disagree the transcript level is the one that says what the model actually contains.

This is gffcompare's answer, not the only one. Bambu can assign a parent gene by exonic overlap while gffcompare could assign it based on splice junctions, so at a nested locus, a model carrying one complete intron from each gets a different parent from each tool. The `compared_` fields are gffcompare's; Bambu's is the `gene_id` on the GTF.

```{r}
#| label: prep-ref-biotype
#| include: false

REF_LEVEL_LABELS <- c(ref_gene       = "compared gene biotype",
                      ref_transcript = "compared transcript biotype")

# Intergenic models are excluded: they were compared against nothing, so a
# "no reference" bar spanning the whole category would say nothing about the
# annotation.
#
# ref_gene and ref_transcript below are local long-format keys, not columns of the
# metadata: REF_LEVEL_LABELS maps them and pivot_longer consumes them three lines
# down. They keep their names.
ref_bt_long <- NULL
if (all(c("compared_gene_biotype", "compared_transcript_biotype") %in% names(novel_tx))) {
  tidy_bt <- function(x) {
    x <- as.character(x)
    x[is.na(x) | !nzchar(x)] <- "no reference"
    x
  }
  ref_bt_long <- novel_tx %>%
    filter(!is.na(class_code), class_code != "u") %>%
    mutate(ref_gene       = tidy_bt(compared_gene_biotype),
           ref_transcript = tidy_bt(compared_transcript_biotype)) %>%
    select(qry_id, class_code, biotype, classification, ref_gene, ref_transcript) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(ref_gene, ref_transcript),
                 names_to = "level", values_to = "ref_biotype") %>%
    mutate(level = unname(REF_LEVEL_LABELS[level]))
}
has_ref_bt <- !is.null(ref_bt_long) && nrow(ref_bt_long) > 0

# Class codes that share splice structure with a reference transcript, and the
# categories that actually have any. Filtering here rather than skipping inside the
# loop keeps the panel count equal to length(related_cats), which is what the
# subfigure lettering counts off.
RELATED_CODES <- c("j", "k", "o", "y", "m", "n")

related_cats <- character(0)
if (has_ref_bt) {
  related_cats <- unname(NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS)
  related_cats <- related_cats[vapply(related_cats, function(cn)
    any(ref_bt_long$biotype == cn & ref_bt_long$class_code %in% RELATED_CODES),
    logical(1))]
}
has_related <- length(related_cats) > 0

# Lollipop inputs, built here so the figure chunks can size themselves.
lnc_ix <- if (has_ref_bt) {
  ref_bt_long %>%
    filter(biotype == "novel lncRNA candidate", class_code %in% c("i", "x")) %>%
    count(level, classification, ref_biotype, name = "count")
} else NULL
has_lnc_ix <- !is.null(lnc_ix) && nrow(lnc_ix) > 0
# One lollipop row per (reference level, reference biotype) actually observed.
h_lnc_ix   <- if (has_lnc_ix) {
  lollipop_height(nrow(dplyr::distinct(lnc_ix, level, ref_biotype)), base = 1.8)
} else 3

related_counts <- if (has_related) {
  ref_bt_long %>%
    filter(class_code %in% RELATED_CODES, biotype %in% related_cats) %>%
    count(biotype, level, classification, ref_biotype, name = "count")
} else NULL
# One figure per category, each sized to its own rows (reference biotypes) and
# columns (classifications). A shared size stretched a 3-row panel to the height
# of a 10-row one and squeezed a 6-column one into the width of a 4-column one.
related_size <- if (has_related) {
  related_counts %>%
    dplyr::group_by(biotype) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      h = lollipop_height(dplyr::n_distinct(paste(level, ref_biotype)),
                          base = 1.9, per = 0.22),
      w = lollipop_width(dplyr::n_distinct(classification), ref_biotype),
      .groups = "drop")
} else NULL

if (has_lnc_ix) {
  w_lnc_ix <- lollipop_width(dplyr::n_distinct(lnc_ix$classification), lnc_ix$ref_biotype)
  h_lnc_ix <- lollipop_height(nrow(dplyr::distinct(lnc_ix, level, ref_biotype)),
                              base = 1.9, per = 0.22)
} else {
  w_lnc_ix <- 7.5
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-lnc-ix-ref-biotype
#| fig-cap: "**Reference biotypes behind the intronic and antisense novel lncRNA candidates.** Class codes `i` and `x` become lncRNA candidates on the coding prediction alone, whatever the reference gene is, so this figure says what those references actually were. One column per classification, each with its own count axis; the upper row compares against the reference gene's biotype, the lower row against the reference transcript's. Each row lists only the reference biotypes observed at that level, and a hollow point labelled 0 is a biotype seen for another classification but not this one."
#| eval: !expr has_ref_bt
#| fig-width: !expr w_lnc_ix
#| fig-height: !expr h_lnc_ix

if (has_lnc_ix) {
  plot_count_lollipop(
    lnc_ix, x = ref_biotype, y = classification, facet = "level",
    title = "Novel lncRNA candidates: intronic and antisense",
    x_lab = "Reference biotype", count_lab = "Candidates",
    colours = unname(NOVEL_COLOURS["novel lncRNA candidate"]))
} else {
  cat("No intronic or antisense novel lncRNA candidates in this run.\n")
}
```

These class codes share splice structure with a reference transcript, so the reference gene's biotype is part of how they are routed. One tab per routed category.

```{r}
#| label: related-ref-biotype
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
#| eval: !expr has_related

# One child chunk per category, so each figure gets its own width and height.
related_tabs <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(related_size)), function(k) {
  cn <- as.character(related_size$biotype[k])
  knitr::knit_child(text = c(
    sprintf("##### %s", cn), "",
    "```{r}",
    sprintf("#| label: fig-related-ref-biotype-%d", k),
    sprintf("#| fig-cap: \"**Reference biotypes behind the %s calls.** One column per classification, each with its own count axis; the upper row compares against the reference gene's biotype, the lower row against the reference transcript's. A hollow point labelled 0 is a reference biotype seen for another classification but not this one.\"", cn),
    sprintf("#| fig-width: %.2f", related_size$w[k]),
    sprintf("#| fig-height: %.2f", related_size$h[k]),
    sprintf("plot_count_lollipop(filter(related_counts, biotype == %s),", deparse(cn)),
    "  x = ref_biotype, y = classification, facet = \"level\",",
    sprintf("  title = %s, x_lab = \"Reference biotype\", count_lab = \"Transcripts\",", deparse(cn)),
    sprintf("  colours = unname(palette_for(%s, NOVEL_COLOURS)))", deparse(cn)),
    "```", ""), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE)
})
cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
cat(unlist(related_tabs), sep = "\n")
cat("\n:::\n\n")
```

#### Bambu Transcript Classification

A class code describes a novel model's relationship to the reference transcript it was matched against. However, Bambu's `txClassDescription` provides an additional layer of detail by specifying **which part of the model was not already in the annotation**. The novelty may involve a new first exon, a novel splice junction, or even an entirely unannotated gene.

This distinction matters because identical class codes can represent very different biological observations. For instance, a model classified as`j` due only to a `newLastExon` is not equivalent to a `j` model labeled `allNew`. Both receive the same class code, but the extent and nature of their novelty differ substantially.

In addition, `txClassDescription` values are not mutually exclusive. A single model can be annotated with multiple novelty features, such as`newFirstJunction:newJunction:newFirstExon`. These labels should therefore be interpreted as a set of novel attributes rather than as a single categorical assignment.

```{r}
#| label: bambu-class-prep
#| include: false

# One row per (transcript, class). Split on the colon rather than matching
# substrings: "newJunction" is a substring of "newLastJunction", so grepl would
# count every newLastJunction model twice.
bambu_class_sets <- NULL
BAMBU_CLASSES    <- character(0)

if ("BambuTxClass" %in% names(novel_tx)) {
  has_class <- !is.na(novel_tx$BambuTxClass) & nzchar(novel_tx$BambuTxClass)

  if (any(has_class)) {
    bc <- novel_tx[has_class, , drop = FALSE]
    class_list    <- strsplit(as.character(bc$BambuTxClass), ":", fixed = TRUE)
    BAMBU_CLASSES <- sort(unique(trimws(unlist(class_list))))

    for (cl in BAMBU_CLASSES) {
      bc[[cl]] <- vapply(class_list, function(x) cl %in% trimws(x), logical(1))
    }
    bc$novel_category <- novel_levels(bc$biotype)
    bambu_class_sets  <- bc
  }
}

# An UpSet over one set is a single bar. Below two, the lollipop and the table
# carry the section on their own.
has_bambu_class <- !is.null(bambu_class_sets) && length(BAMBU_CLASSES) >= 2

# --- Bambu class crossed with the gffcompare classification -------------------
# Long form, so a model carrying two classes is counted under both. That makes the
# column totals exceed the number of models, which is what a set membership means
# and is stated in the caption.
bambu_class_cross      <- NULL
has_bambu_class_cross  <- FALSE

bambu_class_table     <- NULL
has_bambu_class_table <- FALSE

if (!is.null(bambu_class_sets)) {
  bambu_long <- bambu_class_sets %>%
    select(qry_id, classification, novel_category, any_of("BambuNDR"),
           all_of(BAMBU_CLASSES)) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = all_of(BAMBU_CLASSES),
                 names_to = "bambu_class", values_to = "carries") %>%
    filter(carries)

  if (nrow(bambu_long)) {
    bambu_class_cross <- bambu_long %>%
      count(novel_category, classification, bambu_class, name = "count")
    has_bambu_class_cross <- TRUE

    # NDR is Bambu's per-model score, so a median over a class says how confidently
    # that whole kind of model was called.
    bambu_class_table <- bambu_long %>%
      group_by(`Bambu class` = bambu_class) %>%
      summarise(
        Models = dplyr::n(),
        `Median NDR` = if (!"BambuNDR" %in% names(bambu_long) ||
                           all(is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(BambuNDR))))) {
          NA_character_
        } else {
          sprintf("%.3f", median(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(BambuNDR)), na.rm = TRUE))
        },
        .groups = "drop") %>%
      arrange(dplyr::desc(Models))
    has_bambu_class_table <- nrow(bambu_class_table) > 0
  }
}

h_bambu_cross <- if (has_bambu_class_cross) {
  # Bambu classes as columns, most common first.
  bambu_class_cross$bambu_class <- forcats::fct_reorder(
    bambu_class_cross$bambu_class, bambu_class_cross$count, .fun = sum, .desc = TRUE)
  lollipop_height(nrow(dplyr::distinct(bambu_class_cross, novel_category, classification)),
                  base = 2)
} else 3
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bambu-class-upset
#| fig-cap: "**Which parts of each novel model were new to the annotation.** Each bar is one exact combination of Bambu transcript classes; the dot matrix below names it. Bars are stacked by the category the model was routed into, and set sizes on the right give how many models carry each class in total. A model with several filled dots needed more than one novel feature to be built."
#| eval: !expr has_bambu_class
#| fig-width: 7.6
#| fig-height: 5

plot_upset(
  bambu_class_sets,
  sets        = BAMBU_CLASSES,
  fill_col    = "novel_category",
  fill_values = NOVEL_COLOURS,
  title    = "Bambu transcript classes",
  subtitle = sprintf("%s novel models carrying a class",
                     format(nrow(bambu_class_sets), big.mark = ",")))
```

  cat("No novel model carries a Bambu transcript class in this run. ",
      "`BambuTxClass` is read from the assembly's `SummarizedExperiment`; ",

The two vocabularies are not redundant, and where they disagree is where the interesting models are. The figure below crosses them.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bambu-class-vs-code
#| fig-cap: "**Bambu transcript class against gffcompare classification.** One column per Bambu class (most common first), each with its own count axis; one row per routed category, listing the classifications gffcompare assigned in it. A model appears once per class it carries, so a row total can exceed the number of models. A hollow point labelled 0 is a classification the category has, but not with that Bambu class."
#| eval: !expr has_bambu_class_cross
#| fig-width: 13

plot_count_lollipop(
  bambu_class_cross, x = classification, y = bambu_class, facet = "novel_category",
  title = "Bambu transcript class against gffcompare classification",
  x_lab = "Classification", count_lab = "Transcripts",
  colours = NOVEL_COLOURS, colour_by = "row", strip_wrap = 12) +
  # Nine columns: Bambu class names are single camelCase words that cannot wrap,
  # so the strip text is set slightly smaller to fit its column.
  theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = rel(0.85)))
```

```{r}
#| label: bambu-class-support-prep
#| include: false

# Read support per Bambu class. Long form: a model carrying two classes is counted
# under both, which is the only honest way to describe a set membership.
bambu_class_support <- NULL

if (!is.null(bambu_class_sets) && exists("bambu_ids")) {
  fl_ids <- if (!is.null(bambu_ids$fullLength)) bambu_ids$fullLength else character(0)
  uq_ids <- if (!is.null(bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped)) bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped else character(0)

  bambu_class_support <- bambu_class_sets %>%
    select(qry_id, novel_category, all_of(BAMBU_CLASSES)) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = all_of(BAMBU_CLASSES),
                 names_to = "bambu_class", values_to = "carries") %>%
    filter(carries) %>%
    mutate(`full-length support` = qry_id %in% fl_ids,
           `unique support`      = qry_id %in% uq_ids) %>%
    group_by(bambu_class) %>%
    summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
              `full-length` = mean(`full-length support`),
              `unique`      = mean(`unique support`),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(`full-length`, `unique`),
                 names_to = "measure", values_to = "fraction")

  if (!nrow(bambu_class_support)) bambu_class_support <- NULL
}

has_bambu_class_support <- !is.null(bambu_class_support)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bambu-class-support
#| fig-cap: "**Read support by Bambu transcript class.** The fraction of models in each class that appear in Bambu's full-length and unique count matrices. A class whose models are rarely spanned end to end was built from reads that did not cover it, whatever its class code says."
#| eval: !expr has_bambu_class_support

ggplot(bambu_class_support,
       aes(x = reorder(bambu_class, -n), y = fraction, fill = measure)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * fraction)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), vjust = -0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.08), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                     labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", begin = 0.15, end = 0.75) +
  labs(title = "Read support by Bambu transcript class",
       subtitle = "Fraction of models in each class carrying each kind of support",
       x = NULL, y = "Models with this support", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
```

#### Read support behind the lncRNA candidates

Full-length and unique support are both subsets of total, so a candidate holds both, one, or neither. The combination worth finding is **neither**: those candidates were quantified entirely from expectation-maximisation over reads that never spanned them and were never unambiguous.

```{r}

#| include: false

  filter(biotype == "novel lncRNA candidate") %>%
  transmute(classification        = forcats::fct_infreq(classification),
            `full-length support` = qry_id %in% bambu_ids$fullLength,
            `unique support`      = qry_id %in% bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped)
has_lnc_sets <- nrow(lnc_sets) > 0
h_lnc_sets   <- if (has_lnc_sets) bar_height(nlevels(droplevels(lnc_sets$classification))) else 3

Exact counts are in the table below."

### Tracking Evidence {#tracking-evidence}

Novel transcripts are **candidates**, not validated findings. No filtering is applied in this section; every transcript counted in the analyses above remains included. The purpose is not to remove models, but to identify those that carry potential warning signs, ensuring that transcript counts are interpreted in the context of the evidence supporting them.

The evidence considered here is structural. It includes splice architecture, the presence or absence of transcripts in Bambu's full-length and unique count matrices, and the transcript's class code relative to the reference annotation.

**Sense-intronic** candidates are the one category that cannot be resolved by these criteria alone. A transcript located entirely within an intron of a host gene and transcribed from the same strand is sequence-identical to a portion of the host gene's unspliced precursor RNA. As a result, count-based evidence cannot reliably distinguish an independent transcript from incompletely processed host-gene transcription. These candidates are therefore examined individually in [Genomic Context].

  [Genomic Context]: #genomic-context

```{r}
#| label: context-prep
#| echo: false


novel_nc <- read_csv_safe(params$novel_non_coding_meta)
```

#### Which warning signs occur together

Individual warning signs are common. What matters is whether they **occur in the same candidate.**

Each bar represents one exact combination of warning signs. Candidates carrying multiple signs are often the highest-priority cases for inspection.

All sets are threshold-free, defined only by membership or a count of zero. Combinations with no candidates are omitted; the counts below the figure indicate which were absent.

```{r}
#| label: evidence-sets-prep
#| include: false

evidence_sets <- NULL

if (exists("novel_tx") && nrow(novel_tx)) {
  # Membership of Bambu's matrices: a zero/non-zero fact rather than a threshold
  # on a fraction.
  fl_ids <- if (exists("bambu_ids") && !is.null(bambu_ids$fullLength)) {
    bambu_ids$fullLength
  } else {
    character(0)
  }
  uq_ids <- if (exists("bambu_ids") && !is.null(bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped)) {
    bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped
  } else {
    character(0)
  }

  evidence_sets <- novel_tx %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      `mono-exonic`            = !is.na(exon) & exon == "mono-exonic",
      `no full-length support` = !(qry_id %in% fl_ids),
      `no unique support`      = !(qry_id %in% uq_ids),
      `sense intronic`         = grepl("^sense intronic", classification),
      novel_category           = novel_levels(biotype)
    )

  if (!nrow(evidence_sets)) evidence_sets <- NULL
}

EVIDENCE_SIGNS <- c("mono-exonic", "no full-length support", "no unique support",
                    "sense intronic")

# How many candidates carry each sign, zeros included. Bambu calls novel isoforms
# from full-length read classes, so on most runs every novel model is in both the
# full-length and the unique matrix and those two sets are empty. ComplexUpset drops
# an empty set from the matrix, so the sizes are reported in text underneath -- a
# sign nothing carries is a result, not a gap in the figure.
EVIDENCE_SIGN_SIZES <- if (is.null(evidence_sets)) integer(0) else {
  vapply(EVIDENCE_SIGNS, function(s) sum(evidence_sets[[s]], na.rm = TRUE), integer(1))
}
EVIDENCE_SIGNS_DRAWN <- names(EVIDENCE_SIGN_SIZES)[EVIDENCE_SIGN_SIZES > 0]

# One set left cannot make an intersection matrix worth drawing, and none at all
# would error.
has_evidence_sets <- !is.null(evidence_sets) && length(EVIDENCE_SIGNS_DRAWN) >= 2

# Candidates carrying none of the drawn signs. Usually the vast majority, and as a
# bar it flattens every combination that matters, so it is stated in the subtitle
# rather than drawn.
n_evidence_clean <- if (has_evidence_sets) {
  sum(rowSums(as.matrix(as.data.frame(evidence_sets[EVIDENCE_SIGNS_DRAWN])),
              na.rm = TRUE) == 0)
} else 0
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-evidence-upset
#| fig-cap: "**Structural warning signs among novel candidates.** Each bar is one exact combination; the dot matrix below names it, filled dots marking the signs that combination carries. Bars are stacked by routed category, and set sizes on the right give how many candidates carry each sign in total. Candidates carrying none of the signs are counted in the subtitle rather than drawn, since that bar would dwarf the rest. A sign carried by no candidate at all is not drawn."
#| eval: !expr has_evidence_sets
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.2

# Only the sets that anyone is in. ComplexUpset drops an empty set from the matrix
# anyway, and passing one makes the figure silently disagree with its own caption.
plot_upset(
  evidence_sets,
  sets        = EVIDENCE_SIGNS_DRAWN,
  fill_col    = "novel_category",
  fill_values = NOVEL_COLOURS,
  show_empty  = FALSE,
  title       = "Structural warning signs",
  subtitle    = sprintf("%s candidates; %s carry none of these signs (not drawn)",
                        scales::comma(nrow(evidence_sets)),
                        scales::comma(n_evidence_clean)))
```

```{r}
#| label: evidence-upset-note
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if (!is.null(evidence_sets)) {
  n_tot <- nrow(evidence_sets)

  tab <- data.frame(
    Sign       = names(EVIDENCE_SIGN_SIZES),
    Candidates = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)",
                         format(unname(EVIDENCE_SIGN_SIZES), big.mark = ","),
                         100 * unname(EVIDENCE_SIGN_SIZES) / n_tot),
    check.names      = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  cat(knitr::kable(tab, format = "markdown", row.names = FALSE), sep = "\n")

  mat <- as.matrix(as.data.frame(evidence_sets[EVIDENCE_SIGNS]))
  mat[is.na(mat)] <- FALSE
  n_clean <- sum(rowSums(mat) == 0)

  cat(sprintf("\n\n**%s** of %s candidates carry none of these signs.\n",
              format(n_clean, big.mark = ","), format(n_tot, big.mark = ",")))

  empty <- names(EVIDENCE_SIGN_SIZES)[EVIDENCE_SIGN_SIZES == 0]
  if (length(empty)) {
    cat(sprintf(paste("\nNo candidate carries %s, so %s not drawn above. Bambu calls",
                      "novel isoforms from full-length read classes, so a novel model",
                      "missing from either matrix is the exception rather than the rule;",
                      "the fractions behind those matrices are in the next figure.\n"),
                paste(sprintf("*%s*", empty), collapse = " or "),
                if (length(empty) == 1) "that set is" else "those sets are"))
  }
}
```

#### Full-length and uniquely-mapped support

Per transcript: For each transcript, we quantify total supporting reads, reads spanning its complete structure, and uniquely mapped reads. Together, these metrics distinguish support for the transcript model itself from signal arising from partially \*overlapping transcripts.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Read the low tail, not the high one

A novel model's boundaries were placed **by** the reads now counted against it, so a high full-length fraction restates how the model was built rather than testing it. The informative direction is the **low** tail: a candidate whose reads mostly fail to span it is a fragment of something longer.
:::

```{r}
#| label: support-prep
#| echo: false

# Per-transcript totals across all samples. The first column is the transcript id
# and every numeric column after it is one sample.
read_support <- function(path, label) {
  df <- tryCatch(read.delim(path, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(df) || !nrow(df)) return(NULL)
  num <- df[, vapply(df, is.numeric, logical(1)), drop = FALSE]
  if (!ncol(num)) return(NULL)
  out <- data.frame(transcript_id = as.character(df[[1]]),
                    value = rowSums(num, na.rm = TRUE),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(out)[2] <- label
  out
}

sup_total <- read_support(params$counts_transcript,    "reads_total")
sup_full  <- read_support(params$fl_counts_transcript, "reads_full_length")
sup_uniq  <- read_support(params$u_counts_transcript,  "reads_unique")

support <- NULL
if (!is.null(sup_total) && !is.null(sup_full) && !is.null(sup_uniq)) {
  support <- sup_total %>%
    inner_join(sup_full, by = "transcript_id") %>%
    inner_join(sup_uniq, by = "transcript_id") %>%
    inner_join(novel_tx[, c("qry_id", "class_code", "biotype", "classification",
                            "exon")],
               by = c("transcript_id" = "qry_id")) %>%
    filter(reads_total > 0) %>%
    mutate(full_length_fraction = reads_full_length / reads_total,
           unique_fraction      = reads_unique      / reads_total,
           # `biotype` already holds the routed category's display label, so the
           # split here uses the same names as every other figure in this section.
           novel_category = factor(biotype,
                                   levels = c(unname(NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS),
                                              "novel (unclassified)")))
  if (!nrow(support)) support <- NULL
}

has_support <- !is.null(support)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-support-fraction
#| fig-cap: "**Full-length and uniquely-mapped read support for novel transcripts, split by routed category.** Columns are the two support measures, rows the three categories, and the x axis the classification, with mono- and multi-exonic models side by side. Low full-length support means the reads behind a call do not span it; low unique support means those reads are compatible with other transcripts too, so the count came largely from expectation-maximisation rather than from unambiguous evidence."
#| eval: !expr has_support
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.2

support_long <- support %>%
  select(novel_category, classification, exon,
         full_length_fraction, unique_fraction) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(full_length_fraction, unique_fraction),
               names_to = "measure", values_to = "fraction") %>%
  mutate(measure = recode(measure,
    full_length_fraction = "full-length / total",
    unique_fraction      = "uniquely mapped / total")) %>%
  droplevels()

ggplot(support_long, aes(x = classification, y = fraction, fill = exon)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(novel_category), cols = vars(measure), scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", begin = 0.15, end = 0.75) +
  labs(title = "Read support for novel transcripts",
       subtitle = "Low values mark candidates whose supporting reads fit them poorly",
       x = NULL, y = "Fraction of supporting reads", fill = "Exon class") +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
        axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-support-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Median read support by novel transcript category and class code."
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr has_support

support %>%
  group_by(biotype, class_code) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `median full-length` = sprintf("%.2f", median(full_length_fraction)),
            `median unique`      = sprintf("%.2f", median(unique_fraction)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(biotype, class_code) %>%
  knitr::kable(format = "markdown")
```

#### What the predicted non-coding category holds

```{r}
#| label: non-coding-note
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if (is.null(novel_nc)) {
  cat("No models were routed to the predicted non-coding category in this run.\n")
} else {
  by_class <- sort(table(novel_nc$classification), decreasing = TRUE)
  class_txt <- paste(sprintf("%s (%d)", names(by_class), as.integer(by_class)),
                     collapse = ", ")

  hosts <- sort(table(novel_nc$compared_gene_biotype, useNA = "ifany"), decreasing = TRUE)
  host_names <- names(hosts)
  host_names[is.na(host_names)] <- "no reference gene"
  host_txt <- paste(sprintf("%s (%d)", host_names, as.integer(hosts)), collapse = ", ")

  cat('::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}\n')
  cat("## Composition of this category\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("**%s** models are predicted non-coding and share splice structure with a reference gene that is not an lncRNA.\n\n",
              format(nrow(novel_nc), big.mark = ",")))
  cat(sprintf("By classification: %s.\n\n", class_txt))
  cat(sprintf("By reference gene biotype: %s.\n\n", host_txt))
  cat("No coding potential, at a locus that is not a non-coding gene: consistent with an unproductive isoform of the reference gene, and equally with a genuine non-coding transcript sharing the locus. The category names what is known without choosing between them. Full table in `novel_non_coding_metadata.csv`.\n")
  cat("\n:::\n")
}
```

## Genomic Context {#genomic-context}

Coverage and transcript models drawn together at selected loci. The bigWig tracks behind these figures are published alongside the report, so any region can be opened in IGV to explore beyond the windows chosen here.

```{r}
#| label: genomic-context-prep
#| echo: false

gc_clean   <- read_csv_safe(params$genomic_context_candidates)
gc_flagged <- read_csv_safe(params$intronic_context_candidates)

# A short tab label. The stratum is three fields joined by pipes -- category,
# classification, reference gene class -- and as a tab it wraps over several lines,
# so two dozen of them read as a wall of text rather than as a row of tabs. The gene
# and the class code identify a panel in a few characters; the full stratum stays in
# the caption underneath, where there is room for it.
if (!is.null(gc_clean) && "label" %in% names(gc_clean)) {
  code <- if ("class_code" %in% names(gc_clean)) {
    ifelse(is.na(gc_clean$class_code) | !nzchar(gc_clean$class_code), "",
           sprintf(" (%s)", gc_clean$class_code))
  } else ""
  gc_clean$tab <- make.unique(paste0(gc_clean$label, code), sep = " #")
}

# A figure is embedded only when its PNG was actually staged, so a stub run or a
# partially failed draw leaves a gap rather than a broken image.
embed_figures <- function(df, file_col, tab_col, caption_fn) {
  # tab_col may name several candidates; the first one present is used. A tab still
  # needs a label when the candidates table predates the preferred column.
  tab_col <- if (is.null(df)) NA_character_ else {
    hit <- tab_col[tab_col %in% names(df)]
    if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_character_
  }
  if (is.null(df) || !(file_col %in% names(df)) || is.na(tab_col)) {
    cat("No figures were produced for this section.\n\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  present <- df[!is.na(df[[file_col]]) & file.exists(df[[file_col]]), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(present)) {
    cat("No figures were produced for this section.\n\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(present))) {
    cat(sprintf("## %s\n\n", present[[tab_col]][i]))
    cat(sprintf("![%s](%s)\n\n", caption_fn(present[i, ]), present[[file_col]][i]))
  }
  cat(":::\n\n")
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

### One example per kind of novel call

One panel per stratum — routed category × classification × reference gene class — taking the richest locus in each, so every panel is the most informative example of its kind. Class code `u` is absent: it is intergenic, with no reference gene to draw it against.

Each panel shows the reference gene's exonic footprint, then every isoform at the locus with novel ones coloured by biotype, then one coverage track per sample on a shared scale.

```{r}
#| label: fig-genomic-context-clean
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

embed_figures(gc_clean, "figure", c("tab", "label"), function(r) {
  ref_bt <- if (is.null(r$compared_gene_biotype) || is.na(r$compared_gene_biotype) ||
                !nzchar(as.character(r$compared_gene_biotype))) {
    as.character(r$ref_class)
  } else {
    as.character(r$compared_gene_biotype)
  }
  sprintf("%s, %s at %s (%s) — %s:%s-%s. %d isoforms, %d novel. Example: %s.",
          r$novel_biotype, r$classification, r$label, ref_bt,
          r$chrom, format(r$win_s, big.mark = ","),
          format(r$win_e, big.mark = ","), r$n_tx, r$n_novel, r$example_tx)
})
```

### Sense-intronic candidates

Each lies inside an intron of its host gene, **on the host's own strand** — the one relationship position cannot resolve, since such a model is sequence-identical to part of the host's unspliced precursor. They are windowed on the **whole host intron**: a window drawn tightly around a truncated fragment looks discrete whatever it is, and the flanking intron is where the difference shows.

Ordered most ambiguous first: unspliced models, then those with no full-length support, then by count.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## What to look for

A candidate that really is host precursor shows coverage running flat across the entire intron and continuous with the flanking exons. A candidate that is a genuine independent transcript shows a discrete block of coverage with quiet intron either side. Nothing upstream has judged these one way or the other — the panel is the evidence.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-genomic-context-flagged
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

embed_figures(gc_flagged, "figure", "qry_id", function(r) {
  host <- ifelse(is.na(r$compared_gene_name) | !nzchar(r$compared_gene_name),
                 r$compared_gene_id, r$compared_gene_name)

  struct <- paste(
    if (isTRUE(r$num_exons == 1L)) "mono-exonic" else sprintf("%d exons", r$num_exons),
    if (isTRUE(r$full_length_support)) "full-length support"
      else if (isFALSE(r$full_length_support)) "no full-length support"
      else "full-length support not recorded",
    sep = ", ")

  scope <- if (is.null(r$samples_quantified) || !length(r$samples_quantified) ||
               is.na(r$samples_quantified)) "" else {
    sprintf(" in %d/%d samples", r$samples_quantified, r$samples_total)
  }

  sprintf("%s inside an intron of %s (%s), on the same strand. %s. %s counts%s.",
          r$qry_id, host, r$compared_gene_biotype, struct,
          format(round(r$counts_total), big.mark = ","), scope)
})
```
